units.tr: The divine religion shines forth both in the doctrine of the saving Word and in the twofold seal of the eternal covenant. It washes with the sacred stream, and it feeds with saving food and drink the offspring won by the precious blood of Christ. These are the sure signs of righteousness and faith, the props of the faltering heart of the godly, and the token of the assembly of Christians, taught with a sincere mind to leave behind the fictitious rites of merit and the spurious rites of the profane.

units.la: DE SACRAMENTIS IN GENERE. Iuxta declarationem Capitis XIX. Confessionis Helveticæ.
units.tr: On the Sacraments in General. According to the declaration of Chapter XIX of the Helvetic Confession.

units.la: THESIS PRIMA.
units.tr: FIRST THESIS.

units.la: INomni vero, genuino & ordinario Sacramento, conditiones quaternæ observandæ sunt: quarum unâ vel pluribus deficientibus, Sacramentum tale appellari nō potest.
units.tr: In every true, genuine and ordinary sacrament, four conditions must be observed. If one or more of them is lacking, the thing cannot be called a sacrament of that kind.

units.la: PRIMA est, ut ab ipso Deo diserté sit institutum: ab eo enim tota Sacramentorum, promissionis divinæ signaculorum, vis & efficacia dependet. Sicut enim solius Dei proprium est, gratiam promittere & fœdus cum genere humano sancire: ita solius Dei promissoris proprium est sigilla fœderis & gratiæ cœlestis sancire; & sigilla ista non nisi ex voluntate & pacto instituentis efficacia sunt in animis credentium. Ecclesia verò non habet potestatem instituendi Sacramentum, vel substantiale quid in Sacramento divinitus sancito mutandi. Deut. 4. 2. Non addetis, nec diminuetis quicquam ab eo, quod præcepi vobis. Deut. 12. v. 8. 32. Non facietis singuli, quod rectum vobis videtur in oculis vestris, sed custodietis præcepta Iehovæ Dei vestri. Iesa. 29. 13. Matth. 15. v. 8. 9. Col. 2. 23. ἐθελοθρησκεία humana in cultu divino repudiatur.
units.tr: The first is that it was expressly instituted by God himself, for the whole force and efficacy of the sacraments, the seals of the divine promise, depends on him. For just as it is the proper work of God alone to promise grace and to make a covenant with the human race, so it is the proper work of God alone, the promiser, to ratify the seals of the covenant and of heavenly grace. These seals are effective in the hearts of believers only by the will and agreement of the one who instituted them. The Church, however, has no power to institute a sacrament, or to change anything of substance in a sacrament divinely ordained. Deut. 4:2: You shall not add to what I command you, nor take away from it. Deut. 12:8, 32: Every man shall not do what seems right in his own eyes, but you shall keep the commandments of Jehovah your God. Isa. 29:13; Matt. 15:8-9; Col. 2:23: self-chosen worship [ἐθελοθρησκεία], human invention, is rejected in divine worship.

units.la: THESIS II.
units.tr: THESIS II.

units.la: SECVNDA est, ut verum Sacramentum habeat signum aliquod elementare, in sensus incurrens, quo mediante res cœlestes ac spirituales, cognoscere & comprehendere possimus. Unde Augustinus Sacramentum Verbum visibile appelappellavit. In simplici prædicatione Verbi, Deus gratiam suam nobis offert & spondet audibiliter: per usum verò Sacramentorum agit nobiscum visibiliter, ut gratiæ cœlestis sigilla, quasi oculis intueri & manibus contrectare queamus. Ad symbolum corporale refertur etiam ceremonia sacramentalis seu ritus externus, qui consistit partim in actione ministri vicem Dei agentis, signum à communi usu separantis, & rei mysticæ significandæ & obsignandæ consecrantis & administrantis, partim in fidelium participatione visibili.
units.tr: The second is that a true sacrament has some elementary sign, perceptible to the senses, through which we can know and grasp heavenly and spiritual things. Hence Augustine called a sacrament a visible word. In the simple preaching of the Word, God offers and promises his grace to us audibly; but through the use of the sacraments he deals with us visibly, so that we may look upon the seals of heavenly grace, as it were with our eyes, and handle them with our hands. The sacramental ceremony, or external rite, also belongs to this bodily sign. It consists partly in the action of the minister, who acts in God's place, separating the sign from common use, consecrating it to signify and seal the mystical thing, and administering it; and partly in the visible participation of the faithful.

units.la: THESIS III.
units.tr: THESIS III.

units.la: TERTIA est, ut genuinum Sacramentum habeat promissionem Dei de salute æterna, signo visibili annexam, non quamvis generalem, verùm speciali analogiâ ornatâ. Hæc promissio est nucleus & succus & veluti anima veri Sacramenti. Unde πολυθρύλλητον illud Augustini: Accedat Verbum ad elementum, & fit Sacramentum. Verbi institutionis divinæ est partim mandatum, quo Sacramenti administratio & participatio præcipitur: partim verò est promissio authoris, unde Sacramenti usus, efficacia & effectus dependet. Sicut fides requiritur ad efficacem & salutarem Sacramenti usum; & fides nititur fundamento Verbi divini: ita absque præmissa institutionis vel lectione vel explicatione in cœtu Ecclesiastico, Sacramentū administrari non debet. Mat. 26. & 28, Act. 2. & 8. & 10. 1. Cor. 10. & 11. Et qualis est ratio sigillorum, quæ nullius sunt momenti, nisi quatenus diplomatibus annectuntur: talis quoque est ratio Verbi & Sacramentorum. Ioh. 15. 3. Puri estis propter sermonem, Ephes. 5. purgavit nos per lavacrum aquæ in Verbo promissum. Et absque Verbo prædicato præmissō, Sacramenta nec promittunt nec obsignant salutem.
units.tr: THE third is that a genuine sacrament has God's promise of eternal salvation attached to a visible sign, not a merely general promise but one adorned with a special application. This promise is the kernel, the juice, and as it were the soul of a true sacrament. Hence Augustine's much-quoted saying: the Word comes to the element, and it becomes a sacrament [πολυθρύλλητον]. Part of the Word of divine institution is the command by which the administration and participation of the sacrament is enjoined; part is the promise of the author, on which the use, efficacy and effect of the sacrament depend. Just as faith is required for the effective and saving use of a sacrament, and faith rests on the foundation of the divine Word, so a sacrament must not be administered in the assembly of the Church without a prior institution, either read or explained. Matt. 26 and 28; Acts 2, 8 and 10; 1 Cor. 10 and 11. And just as the seals, which have no weight of their own, count for something only insofar as they are attached to documents, so it is with the Word and the sacraments. John 15:3: You are clean because of the word. Eph. 5: he cleansed us by the washing of water in the Word promised. Without the Word preached beforehand, sacraments neither promise nor seal salvation.

units.la: THESIS IIII.
units.tr: THESIS IV.

units.la: QVARTA est, ut Sacramentum toti Ecclesiæ destinatum natum sit in perpetuum usum, quandiu videlicet externa Ecclesiæ forma est duratura. Mutatâ enim cultus divini formâ externâ, mutatur quoque Sacramentorum usus. Sic Vet. Test. Sacramenta non habent locum in Novo; in hoc enim externa religionis forma est mutata. Circumcisio data fuit respectu durationis toti Ecclesiæ Vet. Test. quia non tantùm sub Abrahamo & Patriarchis, verùm etiam sub Mose, & posteris ejus, durante œconomia Legali, usque ad tempus correctionis usurpari debuit. Baptismus & S. Cœna toti Ecclesiæ Novi Test. data sunt, duratura usque ad finem mundi. Quæ verò actiones sacræ primordijs tantùm Ecclesiæ Christi in universum mundum propagandæ servierunt, in Sacramentis Novi Testamenti ordinarijs numerari non debent.
units.tr: The fourth is that a sacrament destined for the whole Church is born for perpetual use, namely for as long as the external form of the Church is to endure. For when the external form of divine worship is changed, the use of the sacraments is changed too. So the sacraments of the Old Testament have no place in the New, since the external form of religion has been changed in it. Circumcision was given to the whole Church of the Old Testament with a view to its duration, for it had to be used not only under Abraham and the patriarchs but also under Moses and his descendants, while the legal economy lasted, until the time of correction. Baptism and the Lord's Supper were given to the whole Church of the New Testament, to endure until the end of the world. Those sacred actions which served only the beginnings of the propagation of Christ's Church throughout the world ought not to be counted among the ordinary sacraments of the New Testament.

units.la: THESIS V.
units.tr: THESIS V.

units.la: Sacramentorum affectiones propriæ sunt binæ: tum VNIO; tum etiam MVTATIO.
units.tr: The proper properties of the sacraments are two: union and change.

units.la: VNIO est, quâ signum & res signata coniunguntur relatione mutuâ & analogicâ, & quodam modo unum fiunt, ita ut signo sensibus exhibito, res signata simul fideli cordi demonstretur, obsignetur & exhibeatur. Quam Vnionem Apostolus appellat κοινωνίαν panis & corporis Christi, 1.Cor.10. v.16. Fictitia verò est adversariorum unio, quâ signum essentialiter cum re signata sit coexistens in eodem loco & subjecto, vel quasi res signata in signo sit inclusa, ceu medicamentum in sua pyxide; contentum in suo continente. Hæc unio non est tantùm Verbalis, quæ in nuda similitudine & comparatione unius ad alterum consistat; sed est vera, viva, efficax, dependens ab operatione Spiritus Sancti. Is enim efficit, ut Iesus Christus, etiamsi in cœlis resideat, totus tamen cum omnibus suis beneficijs, nobis in his terris viventibus & credentibus fruendus, non minùs veré & efficaciter donetur & conferatur, quàm signa ipsa in nostros sensus incurrant.
units.tr: Union is that by which the sign and the thing signified are joined in a mutual and analogical relation, and in a certain way become one, so that when the sign is presented to the senses, the thing signified is at the same time shown, sealed and offered to the faithful heart. The Apostle calls this union the communion [κοινωνίαν] of the bread and the body of Christ (1 Cor. 10:16). The union of the adversaries, however, is fictitious, in which the sign is essentially coexisting with the thing signified in the same place and subject, or the thing signified is enclosed in the sign, as medicine in its box, or the contents in their container. This union is not merely verbal, consisting in a bare likeness and comparison of one thing to another; it is true, living and effective, dependent on the operation of the Holy Spirit. For he brings it about that Jesus Christ, although he dwells in heaven, is nonetheless given and bestowed on us who live and believe on earth, wholly with all his benefits, to be enjoyed no less truly and effectively than the signs themselves strike our senses.

units.la: THESIS VI.
units.tr: THESIS VI.

units.la: MVTATIO est, quâ signa Sacramentalia, Verbo Dei & precibus publicis consecrata, ab officio & usu externo, communi, prophano & terrestri recedunt, atque ita ordinatione divinâ mutantur, hoc est, ad finem & usum sacrum coelestem convertuntur atque sanctificantur. In Sacramento nulla fit mutatio substantiæ & propriorum essentialium, quæ efficiatur miraculosâ quâdam vi verborum institutionis, quæ vulgò Transsubstantiatio dicitur; quâ aqua elementaris in Baptismo mutetur in substantiam sanguinis Christi; vel panis & vinum Eucharisticũ in carnis & sanguinis Christi substantiam. Nec etiam fit συνουσία, quâ IN, CUM, SVB signo Sacramentali, revera coexistat res signata, coelestis: videlicet quód in aquâ Baptismi simul existat ipse sanguis Christi, cum efficacia Spiritus Sancti. Qualis vero est modus unionis Sacramentalis, talis quoque est modus mutationis. At ille est totus Spiritualis: Ergo & hic. Spiritualis inquam, tum quia efficitur operatione Spiritus Sancti: tum quia apprehenditur Spirituali organo fidei. Qualis itemunio & mutatio fuit in Sacramentis Vet. Testam. talis quoque est in Sacramentis N. T. quia omnium Sacramentorum est una communis essentia. Atqui illic fuit tantúm relativa, ratione finis & officij. Ergo & hic.
units.tr: A change is that by which the sacramental signs, consecrated by the Word of God and public prayers, withdraw from their common, profane and earthly external office and use, and so are altered by divine ordination, that is, are turned and sanctified to a sacred and heavenly end and use. In a sacrament there is no change of substance or of proper essential qualities, brought about by some miraculous power of the words of institution, which is commonly called transubstantiation, whereby elemental water in Baptism is changed into the substance of Christ's blood, or the Eucharistic bread and wine into the substance of Christ's flesh and blood. Nor is there any coexistence [συνουσία], by which the signified heavenly thing really coexists in, with and under the sacramental sign, namely that the very blood of Christ simultaneously exists in the water of Baptism together with the efficacy of the Holy Spirit. But whatever the mode of sacramental union is, such is also the mode of change. Now that union is wholly spiritual; therefore this too is spiritual. I say spiritual, both because it is effected by the operation of the Holy Spirit and because it is apprehended by the spiritual organ of faith. Just as union and change were in the sacraments of the Old Testament, so they are also in the sacraments of the New Testament, because all sacraments have one common essence. But there it was only relative, by reason of end and office. Therefore here too.

units.la: THESIS VII.
units.tr: THESIS VII.

units.la: Ex gemina illa affectione Sacramentali, emergūt phrases Sacramentales metonymicæ, quibus signo tribuitur nomen rei signatæ; & vicissim. Quó spectat luculentum illud Augustini: Si Sacramenta similitudinem quandam earum rerum non haberent, quarum Sacramenta sunt, Sacramenta omnino non essent. Ex hac autem similitudine ipsarum rerum nomina accipiunt. Item: Solet res, quæ significat, ejus rei nomine, quam significat, nuncupari. Hinc est quod dictum est, Petra erat Christus. Non enim enim dixit: Petra significabat Christum; sed tanquam hoc ipsum esset, quod utique per substantiam non erat, sed per significationem. Item: Hæc enim Sacramenta sunt, in quibus non quid sint, sed quid ostendant, semper attenditur: quoniam signa sunt rerum, aliud existentia & aliud significantia. Epist. 23. ad Bonifat. Et lib. 3. in Levitic. quæst. 57.
units.tr: From this twofold sacramental quality there arise sacramental metonymies, by which the name of the thing signified is given to the sign, and conversely. To this belongs that splendid saying of Augustine: "If sacraments did not have a certain likeness to the things of which they are sacraments, they would not be sacraments at all. From this likeness they receive the names of the things themselves." Likewise: "The thing which signifies is usually named by the name of the thing which it signifies. Hence it is said, 'The rock was Christ.' For he did not say, 'The rock signified Christ,' but spoke as though it were that very thing, which it certainly was not in substance, but only in signification." Likewise: "In these sacraments, what they are is not the point, but what they show; always we attend to this, since they are signs of things, existing as one thing and signifying another." Letter 23 to Bonifatius, and Book 3 on Leviticus, question 57.

units.la: Metonymia Sacramentalis est duplex, alia Subjecti, alia Adjuncti. Subjecti est, quando vel nomen vel etiam propria adjuncta & effecta signi, tribuuntur rei significatæ: Circumcisio est fœdus: Agnus paschalis est transitus: Panis est corpus, Vinum est sanguis Christi: Baptismus est ablutio peccatorum. Adjuncti, quando vox rei significatæ pro signo suo ponitur: Christus est Pascha: Christus est agnus ab origine mundi mactatus; Corpus Christi in Cœna videtur, frangitur, in terram decidit: Labia sanguine Christi rubescunt; Sanguis Christi in Cœna funditur.
units.tr: Sacramental metonymy is of two kinds: one of the subject, the other of the adjunct. It is of the subject when either the name or the proper attributes and effects of the sign are ascribed to the thing signified: "Circumcision is the covenant"; "The paschal lamb is the passover"; "The bread is the body, the wine is the blood of Christ"; "Baptism is the washing away of sins." It is of the adjunct when the word for the thing signified is put in place of its sign: "Christ is the Passover"; "Christ is the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world"; "The body of Christ is seen in the Supper, is broken, falls to the ground"; "The lips are reddened with the blood of Christ"; "The blood of Christ is poured out in the Supper."

units.la: THESIS VIII.
units.tr: THESIS VIII.

units.la: Sacramenta convenienter dicuntur Sigilla promissionis divinæ, quia ex ordinatione & pacto Dei instituentis efficaciter obsignant & exhibent nobis veritatem bonorum spiritualium promissorum. Unde Apostolus Rom. 4. Circumcisionem Abrahamo credenti fuisse sigillum iustitiæ fidei testatur.
units.tr: Sacraments are fittingly called seals of the divine promise, because by the ordinance and covenant of God who instituted them, they effectively seal and exhibit to us the truth of the spiritual goods promised. Hence the Apostle, Rom. 4., testifies that circumcision was a seal of the righteousness of faith to Abraham, who believed.

units.la: Etsi enim Verbum Dei, respectu suæ naturæ prius & notius sit Sacramentis: cum verbum Dei, cujuslibet Sacramenti sit anima; Nobis tamen notiora sunt Sacramenta quam Verbum, quia promissionem gratiæ ex Verbo prædicatam & auditam, oculis nostris intuendam proponunt, clariùs illustrant, efficaciùs confirmant & obsignant. Atque ita sæpius fit, ut causa quæ naturâ prior est, arguat & illustret suum effectum & adjuncta: vicissim vero effecta & adjucta causam cognitioni nostræ evidentius exponant. Sic authoritas, natura & forma essentialis Verbi divini & Ecclesiæ, se invicem reciprocè arguunt & illustrant.
units.tr: For although the Word of God is prior and better known in its own nature than the sacraments, since the Word of God is the soul of every sacrament, the sacraments are nonetheless better known to us than the Word. For they set before our eyes the promise of grace preached and heard from the Word, illustrate it more clearly, and confirm and seal it more effectively. And so it often happens that a cause which is prior by nature proves and illustrates its effect and its accompaniments, while, conversely, effects and accompaniments set forth the cause more evidently to our knowledge. Thus the authority, nature and essential form of the divine Word and of the Church mutually prove and illuminate one another.

units.la: THESIS IX.
units.tr: THESIS IX.

units.la: Hinc duo προρίσματα resultant. Primum: Nulla ceremonia vel actio habet rationem Sacramenti, extra legitimum usum; quando videlicet praeter & extra Dei Verbum instituitur; vel non iuxta Christi institutionem nec ad finem ab authore propositum administratur.
units.tr: Hence two προρίσματα [prorismata, preliminary propositions] follow. The first: no ceremony or action has the character of a sacrament outside its lawful use; that is, when it is instituted apart from and beyond the Word of God, or when it is not administered according to Christ's institution or to the end proposed by its author.

units.la: Sacramenta ergo non prosunt nec conferunt salutem ex opere operato, ut Pontificij afferunt, hoc est, externa ceremoniae administratione, sine fide, sine bono motu animi communicantis & recipientis. Si Dei Verbum, quod est anima Sacramenti, sine fide perceptum nihil prodest, Hebr. 4.2. & gratia salutifera per Evangelium annunciata, non alio instrumento quam fide applicatur, Rom. 4.16. ideo ex fide, ut promissio Dei sit firma: Quanto minus Sacramenta, quae sunt appendices & sigilla promissionis divinae, salutem homini fide destituto conferre possunt? Rom.2.25. Externa carnis circumcisio, hominii infideli, legis divinae transgressori contumaci fit praeputium, ad salutem inefficax, Rom.2.25. Quicquid non ex fide fit, peccatum est. Rom. 14.23. Hebr. 11. v. 6. Impossibile sine fide placere Deo. Plerique eorum, qui ministerio Moysis baptizati fuerant, mari & nube, non placuerunt Deo, 1. Cor. 10. v. 5. Indigne manducantes & bibentes, sibi ipsis judicium edunt & bibunt; rei fiunt corporis & sanguinis Christi. 1. Cor. 11. v. 29. 1. Joh. 5. v. 10. Qui non credit Deo, mendacem eum fecit, quia non credidit testimonio, quod testificatus est Deus de Filio suo.
units.tr: Sacraments therefore do not profit nor confer salvation ex opere operato, as the Papists maintain, that is, by the outward administration of the ceremony alone, without faith, without a good motion of mind in the one who communicates and in the one who receives. If the Word of God, which is the soul of the sacrament, profits nothing when received without faith (Heb. 4.2), and the saving grace proclaimed through the Gospel is not applied by any instrument other than faith (Rom. 4.16), so that the promise of God may be firm by faith, how much less can the sacraments, which are the appendages and seals of the divine promise, confer salvation on a man destitute of faith? (Rom. 2.25.) Outward circumcision of the flesh becomes uncircumcision to an unbelieving man, a stubborn transgressor of the divine law, and is ineffective for salvation (Rom. 2.25). Whatever is not done from faith is sin (Rom. 14.23). Without faith it is impossible to please God (Heb. 11.6). Most of those who were baptized under the ministry of Moses, in the sea and in the cloud, did not please God (1 Cor. 10.5). Whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment upon himself, and becomes guilty of the body and blood of Christ (1 Cor. 11.29; 1 John 5.10). He who does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed the testimony that God has given concerning his Son.

units.la: THESIS X.
units.tr: THESIS X.

units.la: Alterum est: Cum Sacramenta sint sigilla gratiae salutiferae, eorum ergo usus ad salutem necessarius est, non absolute, sed limitate. Semper enim distinguendum est inter substantiam foederis gratuiti, a quo velut a causa procreante salus nostra simpliciter dependet: & inter foederis eiusdem sigilla externa, quibus ius vitae aeternae proprie non est alligaalligatum. Quicunq; enim electi in fœdere illo comprehenduntur, ij vigore promissionis divinæ τῆς ἀμεταμελήτου, ab æterna salute arceri nõ possunt. Multi verò electi, vel infantes præmaturâ morte hinc divinitus evocati; vel adulti impedimento inevitabili, Sacramentorum participatione orbati, nulla ordinationis divinæ violatione & contemptu intercedente, (quod in persecutionibus sub Turca & Antichristo multoties accidit) interna Dei operatione sanctificantur, hoc est, effusi sanguinis IEsu Christi merito à peccatis abluuntur; Spiritus sancti efficacia ad regnum Dei regenerantur, atque ita spiritualiter per fidem in Filium Dei mortuum & resuscitatum, animabus suis nutriuntur ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: The second point is this: since the sacraments are seals of saving grace, their use is necessary for salvation, but not absolutely, only conditionally. For one must always distinguish between the substance of the free covenant, on which our salvation depends simply, as on a procreating cause, and the external seals of that same covenant, to which the right to eternal life is not properly tied. For whoever are comprehended as elect in that covenant cannot be shut out from eternal salvation, by virtue of the divine promise [τῆς ἀμεταμελήτου, "the irrevocable"]. Many of the elect, however, either summoned hence by God through early death as infants, or as adults deprived of participation in the sacraments by an unavoidable hindrance, without any violation or contempt of the divine ordinance intervening (as happened very often in the persecutions under the Turk and the Antichrist), are sanctified by the inward operation of God: that is, they are washed from their sins by the merit of the shed blood of Jesus Christ; they are regenerated by the efficacy of the Holy Spirit into the kingdom of God; and thus spiritually, through faith in the Son of God who died and was raised again, they are nourished in their souls unto eternal life.

units.la: THESIS XI.
units.tr: THESIS XI.

units.la: Sacramenta utriúsque Testamenti differunt ratione accidentis, hoc est, respectu tum signorum, quæ illic cruenta & operosa fuerunt; hic verò incruenta & faciliora sunt; tum modi circa repræsentationem & obsignationem; illa enim Christum venturum eminus & obscurius obsignârunt; hæc verò Christum iam exhibitum comminus & clarius: illa solos Israelitas obligârunt usque ad tempus correctionis; hæc verò omnes gentes obligant duratura usque ad Christi reditum. Fœdus quidem Dei perpetuum & æternum requirere videbatur sigillum perpetuum; verùm non unum & idem numero, licet specie. Externâ enim religionis divinæ formâ in No. Testam. mutatâ, Circumcisio fuit abrogata, juxta Prophetarum oracula, Ierem. 3. v. 16. Ierem. 31. v. 32. Dan. 9. 27. Actor. 15. v. 10. Gal. 5. v. 2. Pascha cum sacrificijs hostiâ Christi in ara crucis consummatum est. Iohan. 19. 30. 1 Cor. 5. v. 7. Atque his abrogatis Baptismus & S. Cœna ordinatione divinâ successerunt.
units.tr: The sacraments of the two Testaments differ in respect of their accidents, that is, with regard to the signs, which under the old covenant were bloody and laborious, but under the new are unbloody and easier; and with regard to the manner of representation and sealing. For the former sealed the coming of Christ from afar and more obscurely, while the latter seal Christ already exhibited, at close quarters and more clearly. The former bound only the Israelites until the time of correction; the latter bind all nations, and are to endure until the return of Christ. Indeed, the perpetual and eternal covenant of God seemed to require a perpetual seal; yet it was not one and the same in number, though it is the same in kind. For when the external form of the divine religion was changed in the New Testament, circumcision was abrogated, in accordance with the oracles of the prophets: Jer. 3:16; Jer. 31:32; Dan. 9:27; Acts 15:10; Gal. 5:2. The Passover with its sacrifices was brought to completion by the sacrifice of Christ on the altar of the cross: John 19:30; 1 Cor. 5:7. And with these abrogated, Baptism and the Lord's Supper succeeded by divine ordinance.

units.la: THESIS XII.
units.tr: THESIS XII.

units.la: Sacramenta verò utrobique conveniunt, tùm ratione autho= authoris, unius & eiusdem Dei, in uno Mediatore: tum substantiae seu materiae internae, spiritualis, obsignatae, quae utrinque est CHRISTVS: tum denique respectu finis, fiduciam in Christum Servatorem confirmantis & obsignantis; participantes ad gratitudinem & obedientiam erga Deum obstringentis; Ecclesiam Dei a coetibus impiorum discernentis. Promissionis Verbum, quo dona spiritualia credentibus divinitus oblata sunt, etiamsi quoad phrasin differre videatur: ubique tamen Evangelij summa de Semine benedicto inculcatur, Gen. 17. v. 7. Matth. 28. 19. Act. 2. 39. Conveniunt etiam utriusque Testamenti Sacramenta, uno & eodem applicationis instrumento, quod est Sola fides. Quicquid enim ab origine mundi electis a Deo promissum fuit, vel Verbo vel Sacramentis; illud ipsum non alio medio quam Fide sibi applicaverunt. 2. Cor. 4. 13. Habemus eundem Spiritum fidei. Rom. 4 v. 3. 24. Credidit Abraham Deo, & imputatum est ei ad justitiam: Quod scriptum est propter nos, quibus quoque imputabitur, si crediderimus in eum. Ephes. 3. 17. Per fidem Christus habitat in cordibus nostris.
units.tr: The sacraments of both Testaments agree: first, in their author, the one and the same God, acting through the one Mediator; second, in their inner substance or matter, which is spiritual and sealed, and which in both is CHRIST; and finally, in their end, which is to confirm and seal faith in Christ the Saviour, to bind those who partake to gratitude and obedience toward God, and to separate the Church of God from the assemblies of the wicked. Although the word of promise, by which spiritual gifts were divinely offered to believers, may seem to differ in phrasing, the substance of the Gospel concerning the blessed Seed is everywhere impressed: Gen. 17. 7; Matt. 28. 19; Acts 2. 39. The sacraments of both Testaments also agree in one and the same instrument of application, which is faith alone. For whatever was promised by God to the elect from the beginning of the world, whether by word or by sacraments, they appropriated to themselves by no other means than faith. 2 Cor. 4. 13: "We have the same spirit of faith." Rom. 4. 3, 24: "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness. Now it was written for our sake also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe in him." Eph. 3. 17: "Christ dwells in our hearts through faith."

units.la: THESIS XIII.
units.tr: THESIS XIII.

units.la: Testamenti igitur Veteris Sacramenta non fuerunt nudi Typi, figurae & signa tantum venturi Christi: verum etiam sigilla efficacia, quibus redemptio nostra per Christum praestanda, credentibus non modo vere obsignata, verum etiam in legitimo usu realiter exhibita & communicata fuit. Absurdissima est adversariorum sententia: Fideles Vet. Testam. habuisse in Sacramentis suis tantum putamina vacua: Novi vero Testam. fideles habere nucleum, Christum ipsum. Qui enim fideles per Christum consecuti sunt remissionem peccatorum & justitiam aeternam: qui Spiritu Christi regenerati & sanctificati fuerunt ad regnum Dei: illi ipsi quoque corporis & sanguinis Christi participes facti sunt: quia nemo beneficia meriti Christi partiparticipare potest, nisi cum CHRISTO capite in unitate corporis fuerit conjunctus. Ioh. 8. v. 56, Abraham vidit diem meum & gavisus est. Act. 4. 12, Nō aliud nomē sub cælo, &c. Actor. 10. 43, Omnes Prophetæ testimonium perhibēt Christo, &c. Actor. 15. 11, Credimus nos servatum iri, sicut & patres nostri. Psal. 31. 1. Rom. 4. 7. Beati, quorum remissæ iniquitates. Exemplo Abrahami, Davidis & aliorū, per fidē in Christū justificatorū probatur. 1. Cor. 10. v. 3. omnes eandem escam spiritualem edisse, omnes eundem potum spiritualem bibisse: bibebant enim ex sequente spirituali Petra: Petra verò erat Christus. Hebr. 11. v. 1, fides appellatur ὑπόστασις τῶν ἐλπιζομένων, quia Spiritus Sancti virtute efficitur, ut illa quoque bona credenti menti subsistant, quæ tamen adhuc futura sperantur. Apoc. 13. v. 8. Christus appellatur agnus, mactatus inde à jactis mundi fundamentis.
units.tr: Therefore the Sacraments of the Old Testament were not mere types, figures and signs of the Christ who was to come; they were also effective seals, by which our redemption to be accomplished through Christ was not only truly sealed to believers, but was also really exhibited and communicated to them in lawful use. The opinion of our opponents is most absurd: that the faithful of the Old Testament had in their Sacraments only empty husks, whereas the faithful of the New Testament have the kernel, Christ himself. For those who through Christ obtained the forgiveness of sins and eternal righteousness, who were regenerated and sanctified by the Spirit of Christ to the kingdom of God, they also were made partakers of the body and blood of Christ; for no one can partake of the benefits of the merit of Christ unless he has been joined to Christ the head in the unity of the body. John 8:56: Abraham saw my day and rejoiced. Acts 4:12: There is no other name under heaven, etc. Acts 10:43: All the prophets bear witness to Christ, etc. Acts 15:11: We believe that we shall be saved, just as our fathers also were. Ps. 31:1; Rom. 4:7: Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven. By the example of Abraham, David and others, it is proved that they were justified through faith in Christ. 1 Cor. 10:3: all ate the same spiritual food and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual Rock that followed them, and the Rock was Christ. Heb. 11:1: faith is called hypostasis of things hoped for [ὑπόστασις τῶν ἐλπιζομένων], because by the power of the Holy Spirit it comes about that those good things, which are still hoped for as future, subsist for the believing mind. Rev. 13:8: Christ is called the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.

units.la: Sacramenta quidem & sacrificia Vet. Testamenti dicuntur elementa egena, inutilia, Col. 2. v. 8. 22. quatenus in se considerata non poterant peccata populi expiare, vel conscientiam ab operibus mortuis purificare: quatenus verò relativè considerantur, ut sigilla promissionum de Christo venturo, eatenus fuerunt organa Sp. Sancti efficacia ad salutem omni credenti. Pari sensu Lex illa Vet. Test. ceremonialis obtinuit umbram futurorum bonorum, Col. 2. v. 17. Hebr. 10. v. 1. αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων: in N. Testamento habent fideles τὸ σῶμα τῆς χριστῆς, metaphorā sumptā à pictoribus, qui primò rudem & umbratilem imaginis formādæ delineationem præmittunt, & postea corpus ipsum vivis imaginibus delineatum, oculis conspiciendum exhibent; quo exhibito, prior illa umbratilis delineatio evanescit: ita Christo jam exhibito, mortuo, resuscitato, in cælos evecto, Lex illa ceremonialis, ut prima delineatio corporis Christi, id est, verae redemptionis per Christum consummandæ, successivè cessavit & denique evanuit. Sacramenta tamen Vet. Test. non fuerunt in legitimo fidelium usu, umbrae inanes, sed sigilla pariter promissionis de κοινωνία corporis Christi efficacissima.
units.tr: The Sacraments and sacrifices of the Old Testament are indeed called weak and useless elements, Col. 2:8, 22, insofar as considered in themselves they could not expiate the sins of the people or purify the conscience from dead works; but insofar as they are considered relatively, as seals of the promises concerning the Christ who was to come, so far they were effective instruments of the Holy Spirit for the salvation of every believer. In the same sense that ceremonial law of the Old Testament held the shadow of good things to come, Col. 2:17; Heb. 10:1: the very image of the things [αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων]. In the New Testament the faithful have the body of Christ [τὸ σῶμα τῆς χριστῆς], a metaphor taken from painters, who first sketch a rough and shadowy outline of the image to be formed, and afterwards display the body itself, painted in living colours, to be seen by the eyes; once this is displayed, that earlier shadowy outline fades away. So with Christ now displayed, dead, raised and carried up into heaven, that ceremonial law, like the first outline of the body of Christ, that is, of the true redemption to be accomplished through Christ, gradually ceased and at last vanished. Yet the Sacraments of the Old Testament were not empty shadows in the lawful use of the faithful, but were equally most effective seals of the promise concerning the communion of the body of Christ.

units.la: THESIS XIV.
units.tr: THESIS XIV.

units.la: Pontificij igitur Sacramentis Novi Testamenti efficacia salutis falsò affingunt, quippe docent, per hæc tanquã per causas veras & immediatas, ex opere operato, iustitiam & salutem æternam conferri: Seu, esse organa per se ἐνεργητικὰ, effectiva, quæ gratiam iustificantem in seipsis habeant, & vi suâ in homine ea percipiente (si non ipso actu plane impius sit, & peccati mortalis obicem ponat) salutem operentur. Quæ sententia pluribus absurdissimis erroribus scatet.
units.tr: The Papists therefore falsely ascribe saving efficacy to the Sacraments of the New Testament. They teach that justice and eternal salvation are conferred through them as true and immediate causes, by the work worked (ex opere operato). Or they hold that they are instruments that are active in themselves [ἐνεργητικὰ], effective, which have justifying grace in themselves and which, by their own power in the man who receives them (unless he is altogether impious in act and places an obstacle of mortal sin), bring about salvation. This opinion teems with very absurd errors.

units.la: 1. Quia gloriam Dei imminuunt quicunque causæ creatæ corporali tribuunt vim penetrandi, sanctificandi, salvãdi animam, & dona spiritualia conferendi; hæc enim ἐνέργεια solius Dei propria est. Psal. 51. v. 6. 9. 12. Tibi soli peccavi: Tu me purifica & lavabor: Tu ô Deus cor mũdum crea in me. Isa 43. v. 25. Ego ego sum, qui deleo iniquitates tuas. Joh. 3. v. 3. Nisi quis e supernis renatus fuerit. Joh. 13. 8. Nisi Ego te lavero. 1 Joh. 1. 7. Sanguis Filij Dei nos purgat.
units.tr: 1. Because those who attribute to a created bodily thing the power to penetrate, sanctify and save the soul, and to confer spiritual gifts, diminish the glory of God. For this activity belongs to God alone. Psalm 51:6, 9, 12: "Against thee only have I sinned. Purge me, and I shall be clean. Create in me a clean heart, O God." Isaiah 43:25: "I, even I, am he who blots out your iniquities." John 3:3: "Unless one is born anew from above." John 13:8: "Unless I wash you." 1 John 1:7: "The blood of the Son of God cleanses us."

units.la: 2. Quia ista sententia pugnat cum proprietate essentiali omnium Sacramentorum in utroque Testam. quibus non alius effectus à Deo est insitus, nisi gratiam vel jam ante collatam vel postea conferendam, tantùm significandi, obsignandi & applicandi; itaut quoties actioni externæ Sacramentali tribuitur vis spiritualis lavandi, regenerandi, salvandi, toties phrasi metonymicâ id, quod externi signi proprium est, rei signatæ tribuatur. Et licet Sacramenta agant, ut causæ organicæ Spiritus Sancti, per quas non minus quàm per Verbum, beneficia Christi nobis donantur, obsignantur, applicantur: non tamen sunt vasa & vehicula gratiæ justificantis, quæ per se & suâ vi, absque fide & bono motu utentis, salvare quenquam possint.
units.tr: 2. Because this opinion conflicts with the essential property of all Sacraments in both Testaments. To these God has implanted no other effect than to signify, seal and apply grace, either already conferred before or to be conferred afterwards. So whenever a spiritual power of washing, regenerating or saving is ascribed to the external sacramental action, the property of the outward sign is by a metonymical manner of speaking transferred to the thing signified. And although the Sacraments act, as organic causes of the Holy Spirit, through which the benefits of Christ are given to us, sealed and applied no less than through the Word, nevertheless they are not vessels and vehicles of justifying grace, which could save anyone of themselves and by their own power, without faith and a good motion in the one who uses them.

units.la: 3. Quia electorum multi in utroque Testamento, fidei & pœnitentiæ gratiâ à Deo donati fuerunt, antequam vel Circumcisionis vel Bavel Baptismi Sacramento Ecclesiæ insiti & initiati fuissent. Abraham in præputio adhuc existens, credidit & fide justificatus est, Gen. 15. v.6. Rom.4. v.10.11. Et Circumcisionem accepit, in sigillum justitiæ fidei, quam habuit in præputio. Cives Hierosolymitani, Act. 2, Eunuchus Dynastes, Act. 8, Paulus è cælis illuminatus, Act. 9, Cornelius Centurio, Act. 10, ante Baptismum fidei & conversionis gratiam divinitus acceperunt.
units.tr: 3. Because many of the elect in both Testaments were endowed by God with the grace of faith and repentance before they were engrafted into and initiated into the Church by the sacrament of Circumcision or of Baptism. Abraham, while still in uncircumcision, believed and was justified by faith (Genesis 15:6; Romans 4:10, 11). And he received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of faith which he had while uncircumcised. The citizens of Jerusalem (Acts 2), the Ethiopian eunuch, a court official (Acts 8), Paul, illuminated from heaven (Acts 9), and Cornelius the centurion (Acts 10), received the grace of faith and conversion from God before baptism.

units.la: 4. Quia denique Scriptura diserté testatur, tum Verbi divini auditum; tum Sacramentorum usum, infidelibus & impœnitentibus, in exitium æternum cedere. Mar. 16. v.16. Qui non crediderit, damnabitur. Ioh.3. v.18. 36. Qui non credit, jam condemnatus est; & ira Dei manet super ipsum. 1. Cor.11. v.27. Indigné edentes & bibentes rei tenentur corporis & sanguinis Domini. 2. Cor. 2. v.16. Fidelibus Evangelium Christi est odor vitæ ad vitam: aliis verò odor mortis ad mortem.
units.tr: 4. Finally, because Scripture plainly testifies that both the hearing of the divine Word and the use of the Sacraments turn to eternal destruction for unbelievers and the impenitent. Mark 16:16: "He who does not believe will be condemned." John 3:18, 36: "He who does not believe is already condemned, and the wrath of God remains upon him." 1 Corinthians 11:27: "Whoever eats and drinks unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord." 2 Corinthians 2:16: "To believers the Gospel of Christ is a fragrance of life to life, but to others a fragrance of death to death."

units.la: THESIS XV.
units.tr: THESIS XV.

units.la: Sacramenta Novi Testamenti genuina sunt, quorum institutio expresso Dei Verbo nititur; quæ constant tum signo externo, elementari, sensibili, cum ritibus in sensus quoque incurrentibus: tum annexa promissione non corporalis alicuius boni, sed spiritualis, de redemptione per Christum præstita: quorum institutio & usurpatio non communis est cum Veteri, sed Novi Testamenti propria; ad seculi usque consummationem duratura. Ecclesiæ primitivæ Scriptores Orthodoxi vocabulum Sacramenti usurpârunt aliquando significatione latiore, pro quovis instituto sancto, in Dei Verbo fundato. Cyprianus existimavit, ablutionem pedum, die illo quo cœna celebratur, in Ecclesia usurpandam esse instar Sacramenti: Fractionem panis à Christo factam, coram discipulis Emaunta profectis, Augustinus appellavit Sacramentum, id est, Symbolum, quo Christus suam resurrectionem discipulis testatam reddiderit, Idem Impositionem manuum, quâ ministri Ecclesiæ in suum munus initiantur: similiter Catechisationem, Psalmorum decantationem, aliquando Sacramentum appellavit, significatione admodum latâ & Catachrestica. Sensu autem accuratiore & magis proprio ea demum pro genuinis & veris Sacramentis Ecclesiæ Christianæ agnoverunt, quæ ab ipso Christo, tum signo visibili analogico, tum annexâ promissione cœlestis & æterni alicujus boni, diserté instituta sunt, ut in Ecclesia peragerentur usque ad seculi consummationem, qualia sunt Baptismus & Sacra Domini Cœna.
units.tr: The Sacraments of the New Testament are genuine when their institution rests on the express Word of God. They consist of an external, elementary, sensible sign, together with rites that also fall under the senses, and of an attached promise, not of some bodily good but of a spiritual one, concerning redemption accomplished through Christ. Their institution and use are not shared with the Old Testament but belong peculiarly to the New, and they are to endure until the end of the age. The orthodox writers of the primitive Church sometimes used the word sacrament in a broader sense, for any holy institution founded on the Word of God. Cyprian thought that the washing of feet, on the day when the Supper is celebrated, was to be observed in the Church in the manner of a sacrament. The breaking of bread that Christ performed before the disciples who had set out for Emmaus, Augustine called a sacrament, that is, a sign by which Christ gave his disciples assurance of his resurrection. The same Augustine sometimes called the laying on of hands, by which the ministers of the Church are installed in their office, a sacrament; likewise catechising and the singing of psalms, in a very broad and catachrestic sense. In a more exact and proper sense, however, they acknowledged as genuine and true sacraments of the Christian Church only those that were expressly instituted by Christ himself, with a visible analogical sign and an attached promise of some heavenly and eternal good, to be performed in the Church until the end of the age; such as Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

units.la: THESIS XVI.
units.tr: THESIS XVI.

units.la: Huiusmodi proprietates Sacramentales non aliis nisi Baptismo & Cœnæ Dominicæ conveniunt. Repudiamus ergo Canonem 1. Sessionis VII. Synodi Tridentinæ: Si quis Sacramenta Novæ Legis, non fuisse omnia à Christo instituta, aut vel plura vel pauciora quàm septem dixerit, videlicet Baptismum, Confirmationem, Eucharistiam, Poenitentiam, Extremam Unctionem, Ordinem, Matrimonium: aut etiam aliquod horum septem, non esse vere & proprie Sacramentum, anathema sit. De duobus genuinis, Matth. 28. v. 19. cap. 26. v. 26. 1. Cor. 11. v. 28. Per unum Spiritum omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus: & omnes una potione potati sumus in unum Spiritum, 1. Cor. 12. v. 13. De cæteris conceditur, quædam illorum fuisse actiones sacras, fidelibus in utroque Testam. usitatas: cujusmodi fuit institutio parvulorum circumcisorum: Poenitentiæ exercitium: Ordinatio Sacerdotum cum certis ceremoniis conjuncta: Matrimonij usus pius & verecundus. Istiusmodi tamen actionibus non conveniunt Sacramentorum Novi Testam. proprietates, suprà enumeratæ.
units.tr: These sacramental properties do not belong to any others besides Baptism and the Lord's Supper. We therefore reject Canon 1 of Session VII of the Council of Trent: "If anyone says that the sacraments of the New Law were not all instituted by Christ, or that there are more or fewer than seven, namely Baptism, Confirmation, the Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Orders, and Matrimony, or that any one of these seven is not truly and properly a sacrament, let him be anathema." On the two genuine sacraments: Matt. 28. v. 19; ch. 26. v. 26; 1 Cor. 11. v. 28. For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, and we have all been made to drink of one Spirit, 1 Cor. 12. v. 13. Of the others it is granted that some were sacred actions, customary among the faithful in both Testaments: such as the circumcision of infant boys; the exercise of penance; the ordination of priests joined with certain ceremonies; the pious and modest use of marriage. Yet the properties of the Sacraments of the New Testament, listed above, do not apply to such actions.

units.la: THESIS XVII. CONFIRMATIONEM baptizatorum Papisticam,
units.tr: THESIS XVII. The Papistical confirmation of the baptized,

units.la: cam e numero gentuinorum Sacramentorum excludimus: 1. tum quia materia & forma eius nec mandatum nec promissionem à Christo habet: 2. tum quia contumeliosa est in Baptismum à Christo institutum; 3. tum quia coniuncta est cum consecratione chrismatis magica & exorcisatione Cacodaemonis; tum 4. denique quia ritum Catechizandi Apostolicum in ceremoniam superstitiosam inungendi convertit. Materia ejus est Chrisma ex oleo & balsamo confectum. Forma ejus est frontis inunctio, addito signo crucis, in nomine S. Trinitatis, cum alapâ maxillae leniter impactâ, ut admoneatur futurae militiae adversus Satanam. Administratio hujus ritus fit manu Episcopi, & applicatur baptizato non infra septimum aetatis annum, plerunque circa festum Pentecostes. Effectus Baptismi proprios, imò ijs feré majores Confirmationi tribuunt. In Baptismo ajunt hominem ablui à peccatis & regenerari ad regnum Dei. In Confirmatione verò hominem baptizatum porrò corroborari, septiformi gratiâ Spiritus S. ad militiam pro Christi gloria obeundam. Certissima verò media, per quae charismata Spiritus S. electis conferuntur, in ijsdem augentur, confirmantur, conservantur, Scriptura sancta tribuit meditationi Verbi divini, S. Eucharistiae, Fidei in Christum, Precationi ardenti, Ephes. 6. v. 13. 14. exercitio serio donorum in mente acceptorum: quae Pontificij inunctioni Chrismatis & crucifactioni falsò tribuunt. Impium est dicere: Oleum & balsamum, antequam ab Episcopo certis verbis consecrentur, in nomine S. Trinit. à Cacodaemone obsessa & occupata esse. Gen. 131. 1. Tim. 4. v. 4. De donis Baptismo obsignatis luculentae extant promissiones, Ioh. 3. v. 9. Rom. 6. v. 3. 4. 5. 1. Cor. 12. v. 13. Gal. 3. v. 27. Ephes. 5. 26. Tit. 3. v. 5. De Confirmationis Chrismate, nullae prorsus.
units.tr: We exclude it from the number of genuine sacraments: (1) because its matter and form have neither a command nor a promise from Christ; (2) because it is an insult to Baptism, which Christ instituted; (3) because it is joined with a magical consecration of the chrism and an exorcism of the Cacodaemon; and (4) finally, because it turns the apostolic rite of catechising into a superstitious ceremony of anointing. Its matter is chrism made from oil and balsam. Its form is the anointing of the forehead, with the addition of the sign of the cross, in the name of the Holy Trinity, with a light blow struck gently on the cheek, so that the candidate is reminded of the future warfare against Satan. This rite is performed by the hand of the bishop and is applied to the baptized not before the seventh year of age, usually around the feast of Pentecost. They ascribe to Confirmation the effects proper to Baptism, or almost greater ones. In Baptism, they say, a man is washed from sins and regenerated into the kingdom of God; but in Confirmation the baptized man is further strengthened with the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit for the warfare to be undertaken for the glory of Christ. The most certain means by which the charisms of the Holy Spirit are conferred on the elect, and by which they are increased, confirmed and preserved, Holy Scripture assigns to meditation on the divine Word, the holy Eucharist, faith in Christ, fervent prayer (Eph. 6. v. 13, 14), and the earnest exercise of the gifts received in the mind. The Papists falsely ascribe these to the anointing with chrism and the making of the cross. It is impious to say that oil and balsam, before they are consecrated by the bishop with certain words in the name of the Holy Trinity, are possessed and occupied by the Cacodaemon (Gen. 131; 1 Tim. 4. v. 4). Concerning the gifts sealed in Baptism there are clear promises: John 3. v. 9; Rom. 6. v. 3, 4, 5; 1 Cor. 12. v. 13; Gal. 3. v. 27; Eph. 5. 26; Tit. 3. v. 5. Concerning the chrism of Confirmation, there are none at all.

units.la: Confirmatio autem vera baptizatorum, cùm ad annos discretionis pervenerint, consistit in institutione circa primordia doctrinae caelestis de accepto Baptismo; de foedere gratiae; de abrenunciatione Satanae; de stipulatione debitae gratitudinis & obedientiae. Ad quam quam profeßionem adhiberi quoque potest impositio manuum, ut testimonium diuinæ promissionis de dono confirmationis & perseue-rantiæ, Act. 8. v. 17. 18.
units.tr: But true confirmation of the baptized, when they have reached the years of discretion, consists in instruction in the first principles of heavenly doctrine concerning the Baptism received, concerning the covenant of grace, concerning the renunciation of Satan, and concerning the pledge of due gratitude and obedience. To this profession the laying on of hands may also be added, as a testimony of the divine promise concerning the gift of confirmation and perseverance (Acts 8. v. 17, 18).

units.la: THESIS XVIII.
units.tr: THESIS XVIII.

units.la: POENITENTIA, quam Pontificij distinguunt in Contritionem cordis, in Confessionem oris, & in Satisfa-ctionem operis, non est genuinum Novi Testam. Sacra-mentum: tum quia communis est fidelibus in utroque Te-stamento; tum quia destituta est elemento seu signo visibili, diuinitus instituto ad fidem confirmandam: tum quia cor-dis contritio ex consideratione Legis diuinæ orta, nisi con-iuncta fuerit cum fiducia misericordiæ diuinæ in Christo, conscientiam consolari non potest: tum quia confessionem Deo debitam, in clandestinam & auricularem coram Sa-cerdote, peccati admissi cum circumstantijs secretissimis enumerationem, velut in conscientiæ carnificinam, conver-terunt: tum denique quia satisfactionem expiatoriam pro peccatis, ex propriis operibus, in Christi Redemp-toris perfectissimum λύτρον contumeliosam exstruxerunt.
units.tr: Repentance, which the Papists divide into contrition of heart, confession of mouth, and satisfaction of work, is not a genuine sacrament of the New Testament. First, because it is common to the faithful in both Testaments. Second, because it lacks an element or visible sign divinely instituted to confirm faith. Third, because contrition of heart arising from consideration of the divine Law cannot comfort the conscience unless it is joined with trust in the divine mercy in Christ. Fourth, because they have turned the confession owed to God into a secret, auricular enumeration of admitted sins before a priest, with the most intimate circumstances, as if it were a torture of the conscience. Finally, because they have built, from their own works, an insulting structure of expiatory satisfaction for sins against the most perfect ransom [λύτρον] of Christ the Redeemer.

units.la: 1. Qui in Ecclesia primitiva, grassantibus persecutionibus, vel apostasiâ & abnegatione fidei, vel alio scandalo gravi, animos fi-delium offendissent, ij in Ecclesiam non recipiebantur, nisi priús ter-nos illos pænitentiæ publicæ actus obijssent, delictum deplorando corde humili & contrito, publicè confitendo & deprecando; pœnas á Presbyterio sibi impositas luendo; non ut earum persolutione Deo pro peccatis satisfacerent, sed ut ejusmodi castigatione carnis fe-rocia domaretur, cæteri quoque ab ejusmodi lapsibus sibi cavere di-scerent, atque hac ratione apud Ecclesiam extaret publicum seriæ pænitentiæ exemplum.
units.tr: 1. In the primitive Church, when persecutions were raging, those who had offended the minds of the faithful, either by apostasy and denial of the faith or by some other grave scandal, were not received back into the Church unless they first had undergone those three acts of public repentance: lamenting the offence with a humble and contrite heart, confessing and begging pardon publicly, and paying the penalties imposed on them by the presbytery. They did this not so that by paying these penalties they might satisfy God for their sins, but so that the wildness of the flesh might be tamed by such chastisement, the others might learn to guard against such lapses, and in this way a public example of earnest repentance might stand before the Church.

units.la: 2. Perperam verò hinc exstruuntur terni quoque gradus priva-tæ singulorum hominum pænitentiæ, quasi erga Deum meritoriæ, pro peccatis satisfactoriæ. Unde distinctio inter peccatum veniale & mortale; Indulgentiæ item & reliquiarum in igne purgatorio defæcatio, inter Pontificios profluxerunt.
units.tr: 2. But from this they wrongly construct three further degrees of private repentance by individual men, as if these were meritorious before God and satisfactory for sins. Hence among the Papists arose the distinction between venial and mortal sin, and likewise indulgences and the purging away of remnants of sin in the fire of purgatory.

units.la: 3. Verbum Dei non aliam pænitentiam requirit, quám quæ co-sistit in seria cordis contritione & dolore, conjuncto cum fiducia fi-liali, quæ acquiescit in Christi satisfactione perfecta; in confessione erga Deum, non quidem speciali illa singulorum delictorum & circumstantiarum, sed in universali omnium prudenter & imprudenter commissorum enumeratione, juxta exemplum Davidis. Psal. 19. v. 13. Delicta quis intelligit? ab occultis me munda. Psa. 51. v. 6. Prævaricationes meas agnosco: Tibi, tibi soli peccavi. Filij prodigi: pater peccavi in cœlum & coram te. Luc. 15. v. 21. Publicani, Luc. 18. v. 13. Deus propitius esto mihi peccatori. Actor. 2. v. 37. Civium Hierosolym. 1. Ioh. 1. v. 9. Si confiteamur peccata nostra, fidelis est, &c.
units.tr: 3. The Word of God requires no other repentance than that which consists in earnest contrition and sorrow of heart, joined with filial trust that rests in Christ's perfect satisfaction; and in confession to God, not indeed that special enumeration of individual offences and circumstances, but a general enumeration of all that has been committed, prudently and imprudently, after the example of David. Psal. 19. v. 13. Who understands his errors? Cleanse me from secret faults. Psal. 51. v. 6. I acknowledge my transgressions; against you, you only, have I sinned. The prodigal son: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. Luke 15. v. 21. The publican, Luke 18. v. 13. God be merciful to me a sinner. Acts 2. v. 37. The citizens of Jerusalem. 1 John 1. v. 9. If we confess our sins, he is faithful, etc.

units.la: 4. Specialem verò illam Confessionem non repudiamus, si quis peculiaris alicujus criminis sensu itapungitur, ut illud Pastori suo exponat, quó solidam consolationem & conscientiæ tranquillitatem, adversus tentationes Satanæ, obtinere possit: cujusmodi confessio cuilibet fideli libera est.
units.tr: 4. We do not, however, reject that special confession if someone is stung by the sense of some particular crime, so that he may lay it open to his pastor, in order to obtain solid consolation and tranquillity of conscience against the temptations of Satan. Such confession is left free to every believer.

units.la: 5. Satisfactio per certas multas præstanda, pænitenti pro redimendis peccatis á Sacerdote imposita, in Christi meritum contumeliosa est: quia unica ejus satisfactio est ἱλασμὸς & expiandis peccatis nostris. Ies. 53. v. 4. 5. Ipse languores nostros verè tulit; ipse vulneratus est propter prævaricationes nostras. Rom. 3. v. 25. Quem Deus proposuit in propitiatorium per fidem in sanguine ejus. 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. Ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris. 1. Pet. 1. v. 19. Redempti pretioso sanguine Agni. Culpâ á Deo gratis remissâ, pœna quoque satisfactoria tollitur: nec justitia Dei duplicem solutionem poscit, unam á Christo præstitam, alteram á nobis præstandam.
units.tr: 5. Satisfaction to be rendered through certain fixed penances, imposed by the priest on the penitent for redeeming sins, is insulting to the merit of Christ, because his one satisfaction is the propitiation [ἱλασμός] for our sins. Isa. 53. v. 4. 5. Surely he has borne our infirmities; he was wounded because of our transgressions. Rom. 3. v. 25. Whom God set forth as a propitiatory through faith in his blood. 1 John 2. v. 2. He himself is the propitiation for our sins. 1 Pet. 1. v. 19. Redeemed with the precious blood of the Lamb. Once guilt has been freely remitted by God, the penalty of satisfaction is also removed; nor does the justice of God demand a double payment, one made by Christ and another to be made by us.

units.la: 6. Afflictiones, quibus credentes & pœnitentes á Deo castigantur, non sunt pœnæ, quibus eorum peccata expiantur, sed vel πυ-δίκα Θεία paterna; vel Δοχιμαστία fidei, patientiæ, constantiæ, ut in Iosepho, Iobo, Davide, Paulo, &c. videre est.
units.tr: 6. The afflictions with which God chastises believers and penitents are not punishments by which their sins are expiated, but either chastening [παιδεία] of a Father, or a trial [δοκιμασία] of faith, patience and constancy, as may be seen in Joseph, Job, David, Paul, etc.

units.la: THESIS XIX.
units.tr: THESIS XIX.

units.la: EXTREMA VNCTIO non est in ordinariis Sacramentis Novi Testamenti numeranda, tum quia eius materia, forma, actio & efficacia Sacramentalis, nullo mandato nec promissione verbi divini præscripta est; tum quia ritus ille illinendi & inungendi ægrotos, non fuit universæ Ecclesiæ in perpetuum usum destinatus; sed extra ordinem communem & ad certum tempus, nec necessario, sed liberé à fidelibus usurpatus; non ut antidoton, peccati reliquias abstergens, & animam adversus terrorem mortis & inferni confortans, sed sanitatis corporalis restitutioni serviens: tum denique quia ritus iste ungendi, ex Iudaismo & Paganismo <bl>κακοζηλία</bl> quâdam in Ecclesiam traductus & cum blasphemâ dæmonum ex oleo & balsamo exorcisatione coniunctus est.
units.tr: Extreme unction is not to be counted among the ordinary sacraments of the New Testament. First, its matter, form, action and sacramental efficacy are prescribed by no command or promise of the divine Word. Second, that rite of anointing and smearing the sick was not appointed for the perpetual use of the whole Church. It was used by the faithful outside the common order, for a certain time, and freely rather than of necessity. It was not used as an antidote that wipes away the remnants of sin and strengthens the soul against the terror of death and hell, but to serve the restoration of bodily health. Finally, this rite of anointing was brought into the Church from Judaism and paganism as a kind of perverse imitation [κακοζηλία], and it was joined with the exorcism of oil and balsam, a blasphemy of the demons.

units.la: 1. Falsum est, quod Pontificij asserunt, hoc Sacramentum esse à Christo insinuatum apud Marcum 6. cap. v. 13. Per Iacobum postea fidelibus promulgatum & commendatum, tanquam firmissimum præsidium sub finem vitæ adversus hostem salutis. Marci 6. cap. recensetur, quid Apostoli in prima sua emissione intra fines Iudææ præstiterint, ut infirmos sanârint, adhibito externo symbolo unctionis olei; quæ actio conjuncta fuit cum dono miraculorum ad tempus duraturo. 1. Cor. 12. absque ullo mandato idem perpetuó faciendi, & absque promissione efficaciæ aduniversam Ecclesiam spectate. In altera generali legatione, Apostoli sanaturi ægrotos, non semper symbolum olei adhibuerunt: verum plurimos ægrotos sanaverunt, aliquando solo verbo; aliquando impositione manuum; aliq. contactu & procubitu corporis, sudarijs, umbrâ: Et olei unctio tempore Apostolorum non fuit præceptum generale & necessa-
units.tr: 1. It is false, as the Papists assert, that this sacrament was indicated by Christ in Mark 6. 13, and later promulgated and commended to the faithful through James as the firmest safeguard at the end of life against the enemy of salvation. Mark 6 records what the Apostles did on their first mission within the borders of Judea, when they healed the sick by applying the outward sign of anointing with oil. That action was joined with the gift of miracles, which was to last only for a time. (1 Cor. 12.) gives no command to do the same perpetually, nor any promise of efficacy, and it does not concern the whole Church. In the later general mission, the Apostles, when they healed the sick, did not always use the sign of oil. They healed very many sick people, sometimes by word alone, sometimes by the laying on of hands, sometimes by touch, by lying prostrate over the body, by sweat-cloths, or by a shadow. The anointing with oil was not in the time of the Apostles a general and necessary precept.

units.la: ria. necessarium. Et ne γρὺ quidem extat de olei illius consecratione atque exorcisatione, certis verbis ab Apostolis concepta.
units.tr: There is not even a word of Scripture [γραφή] about the consecration and exorcism of that oil, framed in fixed words by the Apostles.

units.la: 2. Idem sensus est Verborum Iacobi, de oleo communi, non superstitiose in nomine S. S. Trinitatis consecrato & exorcisato: non animae refrigerio adversus terrorem mortis, sed corporis sanitati recuperandae serviente, cujus olei usus in regionibus orientalibus frequentissimus ad sanationes fuit. Sanationes miraculosae multis obtigerunt quoad corpus, qui tamen internae & spiritualis sanationis non facti participes: e contrario gratia Dei in Evangelio promissa, in multorum animis efficax fuit, licet eorum corporibus nullum signum exhibitum fuerit.
units.tr: 2. The words of James refer to ordinary oil, not consecrated and exorcised superstitiously in the name of the Holy Trinity. Its purpose is not the refreshing of the soul against the terror of death but the recovery of bodily health. The use of this oil was very frequent in the eastern regions for healing. Miraculous cures came to many people as regards the body, yet they did not become partakers of inward and spiritual healing. On the contrary, the grace of God promised in the Gospel was effective in the minds of many, although no sign was shown in their bodies.

units.la: 3. Locum denique Iacobi, pie & salutariter accommodamus ad usum medicamentorum in morbis Christianorum: qui prius admonendi de causa morbi, ut agnoscant peccata, vera cordis fiducia se ad Deum convertant, restitutionem sanitatis ipsius voluntati assiduis precibus commendent, atque ita medicamentis suis pie utantur.
units.tr: 3. Finally, we apply the passage from James, piously and profitably, to the use of medicines in the sicknesses of Christians. Such people should first be reminded of the cause of their illness, so that they may acknowledge their sins, turn to God with true trust of heart, and commend the restoration of their health to his will by constant prayers. In this way they may use their medicines in a godly manner.

units.la: 4. Optimum vero ἀντίδοτον contra mortem & infernum demonstramus in fideli recordatione promissionum Salvatoris, qui Medicus fidissimus est animae & corporis. Ioh. 5. 24. talem non in judicium venturum, sed ex morte transiturum in vitam. Ioh. 11. 25. Ego sum resurrectio & vita. Rom. 8. 1. Nulla condemnatio! Quis accusabit? Quis nos separabit a charitate Dei? Rom. 14. 8. Sive vivimus, Domino vivimus: sive morimur. Et arma illa spiritualia in Deo valida. Ephes. 6. v. 13. &c. 1 Thess. 4. v. 14. 1 Thess. 5. v. 8. 9.
units.tr: 4. We show the best antidote [ἀντίδοτον] against death and hell in the faithful remembrance of the promises of the Saviour, who is the most faithful physician of soul and body. (John 5. 24.) Such a person will not come into judgment but will pass from death into life. (John 11. 25.) "I am the resurrection and the life." (Rom. 8. 1.) "No condemnation!" "Who will accuse?" "Who will separate us from the love of God?" (Rom. 14. 8.) "Whether we live, we live to the Lord, or whether we die." And those spiritual weapons are strong in God. (Eph. 6. 13, etc.; 1 Thess. 4. 14; 1 Thess. 5. 8, 9.)

units.la: THESIS XX.
units.tr: THESIS XX.

units.la: ORDINATIO personarum ad sacram Leiturgiam, septem gradibus distincta, 1. Ostiariorum, 2. Lectorum, 3. Exorcistarum, 4. Acoluthorum, 5. Subdiaconorum, 6. Diaconorum, 7. Sacerdotum; non accenseri debet genuinis Sacramentis Novi Testamenti; tum quia gradus istinullum habent fundamentum & exemplum in Ecclesia Apostolica; tum quia Pastorum ordinatio legitima ad functionem Ecclesiasticam, Veteri Testamento etiam communis fuit cum Novo: tum vero quia ordo iste nō toti Ecclesiæ communis est. (cuiusmodi verum & genuinum Sacramentum esse debet) sed ad certum ordinem clericorum alligatus, exclusis laicis, qui tamen pars Ecclesiæ non postrema sunt: tum denique quia destituta est promissione divinâ, de peccatorum remissione, personæ ordinatæ certo visibili signo, applicanda & obsignanda.
units.tr: The ordination of persons to the sacred liturgy, divided into seven grades: (1) of doorkeepers, (2) of readers, (3) of exorcists, (4) of acolytes, (5) of subdeacons, (6) of deacons, (7) of priests, should not be counted among the genuine sacraments of the New Testament. This is so, first, because these grades have no foundation or example in the apostolic Church; second, because the lawful ordination of ministers for ecclesiastical function was common to the Old Testament as well as the New; and third, because this order is not common to the whole Church (which a true and genuine sacrament must be), but is tied to a certain order of clergy, with the laity excluded, though the laity are no small part of the Church; and finally, because it lacks the divine promise of the remission of sins, to be applied and sealed to the ordained person by a certain visible sign.

units.la: 1. Ordinationem Sacramentalem Pontificij eam esse asserunt, quâ personæ sacræ non modo ad munus prædicandi Evangelium & Sacramenta administrandi, verùm etiam ad celebrandas Missas & ad offerendum pro vivis & mortuis, per certos gradus constituantur: quorum postremum non modo mandato divino caret, verùm etiam cum dignitate victimæ Christi semel in cruce pro credentium sanctificatione consummatæ, pugnat.
units.tr: 1. The Papists assert that sacramental ordination is that by which sacred persons are appointed, through certain grades, not only to the office of preaching the Gospel and administering the sacraments, but also to celebrate Masses and to offer for the living and the dead. The last of these not only lacks divine command but also clashes with the dignity of the sacrifice of Christ, which was offered once for all on the cross for the sanctification of believers.

units.la: 2. In descriptione ordinationis Presbyterorum, Pastorum, Episcoporum, juxta Canonem Apostolicum in Epistolis ad Timotheum & Titum expressum, nulla fit mentio istorum graduum, nec chrismatis, nec olei, nec characteris indelebilis: verùm recensentur necessariæ illæ dotes & virtutes, quibus Ecclesiæ doctores suo gregi prælucere debeant; annexis præceptis salutaribus, quibus in universa sui muneris œconomia, obedire debeant.
units.tr: 2. In the description of the ordination of presbyters, pastors and bishops, according to the apostolic canon expressed in the Epistles to Timothy and Titus, there is no mention of these grades, nor of chrism, nor of oil, nor of an indelible character. Rather, the necessary qualities and virtues are listed, by which the teachers of the Church ought to shine before their flock, with wholesome precepts attached, which they ought to obey in the whole management of their office.

units.la: 3. Inter alias superstitionum & idololatriæ species, quæ in ista ordinatione concurrunt, exercetur horribilis Exorcismus, quo Cacodæmonas ex aqua, sale, oleo, invocato sacrosanctæ Trinitatis nomine exorcizant, ejurant & expellunt. Christus equidem dedit Apostolis potestatem ejiciendi dæmonia ex hominibus corporaliter obsessis, idque virtute miraculosâ. Marci 6. & 16. non autem per demurmurationes magicas, imprecationes, adjurationes, incantationes, quales Pontificijs in usu sunt.
units.tr: 3. Among the other kinds of superstition and idolatry that meet in this ordination, a horrible exorcism is practised, by which they exorcise, abjure and expel evil spirits from water, salt and oil, invoking the name of the most holy Trinity. Christ indeed gave the apostles power to cast out demons from men bodily possessed, and that by miraculous power (Mark 6 and 16), but not by magical murmurings, imprecations, adjurations and incantations, such as the Papists use.

units.la: 4. Ritus impositionis manuum descendit ab actionibus Patriarcharum benedicentium suis filijs & nepotibus, Gen. 48. v. 14. Num. 27. v.18. Moses electurus jussu Dei Iosuam in Ducem populi, imposuit manum suam super eum: & peculiari ritu Sacerdos manum capiti victimae Deo offerendae imponere debuit. In N. Testam. ritus ille liberè fuit usurpatus: ubi charismata illa Spiritus Sancti non tribuuntur actioni impositionis manuum, sed adjunctae precationi & benedictioni, quae quatenus suffulta est promissione divinâ, nequaquam redditur irrita. Hinc ritus ille in Ecclesijs Reformatis, in solenni Pastoris inauguratione asservatur, tum ut is qui ad sacrum ministerium ordinatur, hac ceremoniâ admoneatur, se destinari, consecrari & devoveri muneri sacro, cujus author, protector & conservator sit Deus omni benedictione in aeternum locuples: tum verò ut auditores & spectatores Pastorem legitimè vocatum, debito honoris, amoris & obedientiae officio promptius prosequantur.
units.tr: 4. The rite of the laying on of hands descends from the actions of the patriarchs blessing their sons and grandsons (Gen. 48. 14; Num. 27. 18). When Moses, by the command of God, was about to choose Joshua as leader of the people, he laid his hand upon him, and by a particular rite the priest was to lay his hand on the head of the victim offered to God. In the New Testament this rite was used freely, where those gifts of the Holy Spirit are not ascribed to the act of laying on of hands, but to the prayer and blessing joined to it; and since this is supported by the divine promise, it is by no means made void. Hence this rite is retained in the Reformed Churches at the solemn inauguration of a minister, both so that the one who is ordained to the sacred ministry may be reminded by this ceremony that he is designated, consecrated and devoted to the sacred office, whose author, protector and preserver is God, rich in every blessing for ever; and so that the hearers and spectators may more readily discharge the due duty of honour, love and obedience toward a minister lawfully called.

units.la: THESIS XXI.
units.tr: THESIS XXI.

units.la: Denique MATRIMONIUM Sacramentis Novi Testamenti perperam accensetur, partim: quia commune est, tum Novo cum Veteri Testamento, tum etiam Ecclesiae Dei cum gentibus incredulis: partim quia destitutum est signo elementari divinitus sancito, & promissione applicādi & participandi iustitiam & salutem æternam: (vera enim pietas & sanctitas hominis non consistit in certo vitæ statu, sed in agnitione, fide & timore veri Dei:) partim denique quia Pontificiorum doctrina de Matrimonio, aperta contradictione involuta est; dum illud modó pro mysterio magno extollunt; modó verò ut vitam carnalem Deo exosam, repudiant, & eiusdem usu ordini Ecclesiastico temerarie interdicunt.
units.tr: Lastly, MARRIAGE is wrongly counted among the Sacraments of the New Testament: partly because it is common both to the New and the Old Testament, and also to the Church of God and the unbelieving nations; partly because it lacks an elemental sign divinely sanctioned, and a promise of applying and partaking of righteousness and eternal salvation (for true piety and holiness of man do not consist in a fixed state of life, but in the knowledge, faith and fear of the true God); and partly, finally, because the Papists' doctrine of marriage is involved in an open contradiction, since they at one time extol it as a great mystery, and at another time reject it as a carnal life hateful to God, and rashly forbid its use to the ecclesiastical order.

units.la: Fidelibus in matrimonio viventibus facta est promissio divina benebenedictionis & corporalis & spiritualis ; attamen non propter externam vitam conjugalem, sed propter pietatem cum conjugio cō-junctam, hoc est, quatenus permanent in fide Christi, in charitate & sanctificatione. 1. Tim. 2. v. 15. Cumque Sacramenta instituta sint post lapsum, ut sigilla promissionis divinae de redemptione generis humani per Christum: matrimonium vero ante lapsum, inter homines in statu integritatis viventes, sancitum sit; ergo Sacramentis proprie dictis accenseri non debet. Apostolus quidem Ephes. 5. v. 25. Matrimonium appellat μυστήριον μέγα, non propter carnalem conjunctionem maris & faeminae, sed propter mysticam illam, spiritualem & longe arctissimam copulam, quae Christo cum Ecclesia intercedit.
units.tr: To believers living in marriage the divine promise of blessing, both bodily and spiritual, has been made; yet not on account of the external conjugal life, but on account of the piety joined with marriage, that is, insofar as they remain in the faith of Christ, in love and in sanctification (1 Tim. 2:15). And since the Sacraments were instituted after the fall, as seals of the divine promise concerning the redemption of the human race through Christ, but marriage was sanctioned before the fall, among men living in a state of integrity, therefore it ought not properly speaking to be counted among the Sacraments. The Apostle indeed (Eph. 5:25) calls marriage a great mystery [μυστήριον μέγα], not on account of the carnal union of man and woman, but on account of that mystical, spiritual and by far closest bond which intervenes between Christ and the Church.

units.la: CONFESSIO HELVETICAE CAPUT XX. DE SANCTO BAPTISMO.
units.tr: CONFESSIO HELVETICAE CHAPTER XX. CONCERNING HOLY BAPTISM.

units.la: THESIS XXII.
units.tr: THESIS XXII.

units.la: DOcemus cum Apostolo : Baptismum esse lavacrum aquae in Verbo, quo Christus mundat Ecclesiam, regenerans eam per Spiritum Sanctum. Ephes. 5. cap. v. 26. Tit. 3. v. 5. Hoc est esse Sacramentum a Christo institutum, quo aqua baptizatis in nomine Patris, Filii & Spiritus Sancti, Deus testificatur, se eos recipere in foedus gratiae propter Christum, & sanguine eius ac Spiritu Sancto a peccatis mundare, eosque renovare ad vitam aeternam.
units.tr: We teach, with the Apostle, that Baptism is the washing of water in the Word, by which Christ cleanses the Church, regenerating it through the Holy Spirit (Eph. 5:26; Tit. 3:5). This is to say that it is a Sacrament instituted by Christ, in which water is given to those baptized in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and God testifies that He receives them into the covenant of grace on account of Christ, and cleanses them from their sins by His blood and by the Holy Spirit, and renews them to eternal life.

units.la: Matth. 28. v. 19. Docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine P. F. & Sp. Sancti. Marci 16. v. 16. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit. Ezech. 36. v. 25. efficacia illa donorum Spiritus Sancti describitur metaphora aquae mundae, &c. 1. Cor. 6. v. 11. Et haec eratis quidam, sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis, &c. Ephes. 5. v. 25. 26. Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, & semetipsum exposuit pro ea, ut eam sanctificaret, purgans lavacro aquae per Verbum. 1. Pet. 1. v. 2. Electos sanctificari per ῥαντισμὸν τῆς αἵματος χριστοῦ. 1. Joh. 1. v. 7. Sanguis Filij Dei purgat nos ab omni peccato. Hebr. 9. v. 14. Quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per Spiritum aeternum, seipsum obtulit inculpatum Deo, purgabit conscientiam nostram a mortuis operibus, ad serviendum Deo vivo. Apoc. 1. v. 5. Christus dilexit nos & lavit nos a peccatis nostris, per sanguinem suum.
units.tr: Matt. 28:19: "Teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit." Mark 16:16: "He who believes and is baptized will be saved." Ezek. 36:25: that efficacy of the gifts of the Holy Spirit is described by the metaphor of clean water, etc. 1 Cor. 6:11: "And such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified, etc." Eph. 5:25-26: "Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing of water through the Word." 1 Pet. 1:2: the elect are sanctified by the sprinkling [ῥαντισμὸν] of the blood of Christ. 1 John 1:7: "The blood of the Son of God cleanses us from all sin." Heb. 9:14: "How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works, to serve the living God." Rev. 1:5: "Christ loved us and washed us from our sins by his blood."

units.la: THESIS XXIII.
units.tr: THESIS XXIII.

units.la: In legitimo Baptismi usu, interna actio Spiritus Sancti, per externam ministri non modo significatur & obsignatur, verum etiam exhibetur. Hinc Baptismus recte dicitur peccata abluere, hominem regenerare, salvum facere. Actor. 22. v. 16. Tit 3. v 5. 1. Pet 3. v. 21. Non vi latente vel aquae annexa, qua gratia Spiritualis homini baptizato conferatur ex opere operato: Sed metonymia Sacramentis familiari, qua signo repraesentanti, testificanti, obsignanti & exhibenti, tribuitur id, quod Spiritus Sancti proprium est.
units.tr: In the lawful use of Baptism, the inward action of the Holy Spirit is not only signified and sealed by the outward action of the minister, but is also actually exhibited. Hence Baptism is rightly said to wash away sins, to regenerate a man, and to save him (Acts 22:16; Titus 3:5; 1 Pet. 3:21).
