This is not because some hidden power lies in the water or is joined to it, by which spiritual grace is conferred on the baptized person by the mere performance of the act (ex opere operato). Rather, it is by a metonymy familiar in the sacraments, by which what belongs to the Holy Spirit is attributed to the sign, which represents, testifies, seals and exhibits.

units.la: Actor. 2. v. 38. Petrus ad incolas Hierosolymae, eadem Filij Dei corde contrito lamentates, perspicue locutus est: Poenitentiam agite, & baptizetur unus quisque in remissionem peccatorum. Act. 22. v. 16. Ananias ad Paulum phrasi tropica: Baptizator, ablue peccata tua. Quotquot in Christum baptizati estis, Christum induistis. Gal. 3. 27. Quotquot in Christum baptizati sumus, in mortem ejus baptizati sumus: & sepulti una cum eo per Baptismum in mortem, ut resurrectionis conformatione cum eo quoq; plantati coalescamus. Rom. 6. 4. Tit. 3. v. 5. Deus pro sua misericordia salvavit nos per lavacrum regenerationis & per regenerationem Spiritus Sancti. In his, quod rei signatae, id est, Christi, proprium est, qui solus Ius suo sanguine nos à peccatis purgat & Spiritu suo corda regenerat, tribuitur sacramentali symbolo & sigillo, propter perpetuam analogiam inter signum & signatum. In Baptismo peccata credentibus remittuntur, non ut corruptio naturæ seu prava concupiscentia, quæ peccati materia & fomentum est, prorsus tollatur, verùm ue ijs imputetur ad condemnationem. Rom. 8. v. 1. Sic regeneratio in Baptismo obsignata, non fit simul & semel, sed successivé, de die in diem; & actus ejus continuus durat ad extremum usque diem.
units.tr: Peter, speaking plainly to the inhabitants of Jerusalem with the same contrite heart as the Son of God, said: "Repent, and let each one of you be baptized for the forgiveness of sins" (Acts 2:38). Ananias, in a figurative phrase, says to Paul: "Be baptized, and wash away your sins" (Acts 22:16). "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ" (Gal. 3:27). "As many of us as have been baptized into Christ were baptized into his death, and were buried together with him through Baptism into death, so that, being made conformable to his resurrection, we may also grow together with him" (Rom. 6:4). "God, according to his mercy, saved us through the washing of regeneration and by regeneration through the Holy Spirit" (Titus 3:5). In these passages, what is proper to the thing signified, namely Christ, who alone cleanses us from our sins by his own blood and regenerates our hearts by his Spirit, is ascribed to the sacramental symbol and seal, on account of the perpetual analogy between sign and thing signified. In Baptism sins are forgiven to believers, not in such a way that the corruption of nature, or the evil concupiscence which is the matter and fuel of sin, is utterly removed, but so that it is not imputed to them for condemnation (Rom. 8:1). Thus regeneration, sealed in Baptism, does not happen all at once, but successively, from day to day; and its action continues without interruption until the last day.

units.la: THESIS XXIV.
units.tr: THESIS XXIV.

units.la: Baptismus totaliter consideratus, unus est, Ephes. 4. v. 5. Si verò inter externam personæ administrantis, & inter internam Spiritus Sancti actionem distinguatur, asserimus: unum illum Baptismum geminâ ablutione constare: tum externâ aquæ in sensus incurrente; tum internâ sanguinis ac Spiritus Christi, in Evangelio promissâ. Sic enim Baptismus aquæ á Iohanne administratus, differebat ab interna actione Christi, Spiritu Sancto baptizantis, Ioh. 1. v. 33 Act. 1. v. 5. aquæ Baptismus quo sordes abjiciuntur, distinguitur á stipulatione bonæ conscientiæ, 1. Pet. 3. v. 21. Circumcisio literæ & carnis, á circumcisione Spiritus & cordis differre dicitur. Rom. 2. v. 28. Sic in usu legitimo S. Eucharistiæ, alius est esus & potus externus, qui ab homine fideli fit ore corporeo: alius internus, qui fit ore animæ spirituali, id est verâ fide Ioh. 6. v. 35. Ego sum panis ille vitæ: qui venit ad me, nequaquam esuriet; & qui credit in me, non sitiet unquam.
units.tr: Baptism, considered as a whole, is one (Eph. 4:5). But if a distinction is drawn between the external action of the person administering it and the internal action of the Holy Spirit, we assert that this one Baptism consists of a twofold washing: the external washing with water, which falls under the senses, and the internal washing with the blood and Spirit of Christ, promised in the Gospel. Thus the baptism of water administered by John differed from the internal action of Christ, who baptizes with the Holy Spirit (John 1:33; Acts 1:5). The baptism of water, by which filth is put away, is distinguished from the pledge of a good conscience (1 Pet. 3:21). Circumcision of the letter and of the flesh is said to differ from circumcision of the Spirit and of the heart (Rom. 2:28). So too in the lawful use of the Holy Eucharist, there is one external eating and drinking, which the faithful person performs with the bodily mouth, and another internal one, which is performed with the spiritual mouth of the soul, that is, by true faith: "I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall never hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst" (John 6:35).

units.la: THESIS XXV.
units.tr: THESIS XXV.

units.la: Et quemadmodum Baptismus numero unus á Christo institutus, novi fœderis Sacramentum est initiatorium, circumcisioni substitutum, ita semel tantum administrari & nunquam iterari debet. Baptismus enim semel acceptus, poenipoenitentibus semper manet sigillum gratiae divinae ratum & efficax: sicut ipsius foederis promissio, non tantum universae Ecclesiae respectu, verum etiam singulorum credentium & poenitentium ratione, perpetuam efficaciam obtinet. Etiamsi homo foedus Dei gratuitum peccatis gravibus saepius violaverit, non tamen foederis illius sigillum idcirco est iterandum, vel Baptismus novus homini poenitenti est accersendus, sed efficacia Baptismi semel accepti, per fidem & poenitentiam restaurari debet. Quid tum enim, si quidam eorum fuerint infideles, num incredulitas eorum fidem Dei enervabit? Absit. Rom. 3. v. 3. Si infidi sumus, ille tamen fidus manet, & seipsum negare non potest. 2. Tim. 2, v. 13.
units.tr: And just as Baptism, instituted by Christ once for all, is the initiatory sacrament of the New Covenant, put in place of circumcision, so it must be administered only once and never repeated. For Baptism, once received, always remains for the penitent a seal of divine grace, valid and effective, just as the promise of the covenant itself keeps its lasting efficacy, not only with respect to the whole Church but also with respect to each believing and penitent person. Even if a man has often violated God's gratuitous covenant by grievous sins, the seal of that covenant is not therefore to be repeated, nor is a new Baptism to be sought for a penitent man; rather, the efficacy of the Baptism once received must be restored through faith and repentance. For what follows if some of them have been unbelievers? Will their unbelief make void the faithfulness of God? By no means. If we are faithless, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself. 2 Tim. 2:13.

units.la: THESIS XXVI.
units.tr: THESIS XXVI.

units.la: Obiectum Baptismi est duplex: primum sunt adulti; deinde infantes ex parentibus Christum professis geniti, vel cum parentibus in Ecclesiam transeuntes. Adulti, qui ex Iudaeis & Gentibus, extra Ecclesiae communionem geniti & ad fidem Christi conversi sunt, antequam per Baptismum Ecclesiae inserantur, doctrinae Evangelicae capita solide intelligere & ore profiteri, & ab Ecclesia Baptismum petere debent. Infantes vero, licet fidem actualem & poenitentiam nondum profiteri possint, attamen quia ex foederatis Dei, ex fidei domesticis nati sunt, & iuxta regulam charitatis, in membris Ecclesiae a Christo redemptae & sanctificatae numerantur, non minus igitur, quam pueruli Israelitarum in V. Testam. circumcisi fuerunt, baptizandi sunt.
units.tr: The object of baptism is twofold: first, adults; second, infants born of parents who profess Christ, or who pass into the Church together with their parents. Adults, who are of Jews and Gentiles, born outside communion with the Church and converted to faith in Christ, must, before they are incorporated into the Church through baptism, understand the heads of evangelical doctrine soundly, profess them with the mouth, and ask the Church for baptism. Infants, although they cannot yet profess actual faith and repentance, are nevertheless born of God's covenanted people and of the household of faith, and according to the rule of charity they are counted among the members of the Church redeemed and sanctified by Christ. Therefore they are to be baptized, no less than the little sons of the Israelites were circumcised in the Old Testament.

units.la: De adultis intelligenda sunt: Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit. Mar. 16. v. 16. Agite poenitentiam, & baptizetur quisque. Act. 2. v. 38. Si credis ex toto corde, nihil prohibet te baptizari: cui resp. credo Iesum esse Filium Dei. Act. 8. v. 36, 37. Corde creditur ad iustitiam, ore fit confessio ad salutem. Rom. 10. v. 10.
units.tr: These things must be understood of adults: "He who believes and is baptized will be saved." Mark 16:16. "Repent, and let each one be baptized." Acts 2:38. "If you believe with all your heart, nothing prevents you from being baptized," to which the answer is: "I believe that Jesus is the Son of God." Acts 8:36, 37. "With the heart one believes unto righteousness; with the mouth confession is made unto salvation." Rom. 10:10.

units.la: D
units.tr: D

units.la: Et quemadmodum Dei Circumcisionis initium sumpsit ab adultis, ab Abrahamo jam nonagenario, & porrò ab ejus vernis, maribus domesticis: Tale quoque initium Baptismi in No. Test. fuit ab adultis, qui ex Iudæis & Gentibus colligebantur: progressu verò temporis ipsorum quoque liberi, per Baptismum inter concives Ecclesiæ cooptati fuerant.
units.tr: Just as the circumcision of God began with adults, with Abraham already ninety-nine years old, and afterwards with his young male household members, so too the beginning of baptism in the New Testament was with adults, who were gathered from Jews and Gentiles. But in the course of time their children too were admitted through baptism as fellow citizens of the Church.

units.la: Infantium ergo Baptismus rectè asseritur promissione fœderis, quæ se ad infantes quoque extendit. Gen. 17. v. 7. Actor. 2. v. 39. Angeli eorum intuentur faciem Dei. Sinite pueruios, & ne prohibete eos ad me venire, talium enim est regnum Dei: quos Dominus præterea in ulnas accepit, & manibus impositis eis benedixit. Mat. 28 v. 10. & cap. 19. v. 14. 15. Unde Apostoli integras quoque familias, quarum membra sunt infantes, baptizârunt. Actor. 16. 33. 34. 1. Cor. 1. v. 16.
units.tr: Infant baptism is therefore rightly grounded in the promise of the covenant, which extends to infants also. Gen. 17:7. Acts 2:39. "Their angels behold the face of God." "Suffer the little children, and do not forbid them to come to me, for of such is the kingdom of God"; and the Lord moreover "took them up in his arms and, laying his hands on them, blessed them." Mat. 28:10, and ch. 19:14, 15. Hence the Apostles also baptized whole families, whose members included infants. Acts 16:33, 34. 1 Cor. 1:16.

units.la: Deinde probatur Sacramento Circumcisionis, cui quoad substantiam, remotis ceremoniis & accidentibus, Baptismus in No. Test. successit. Col. 2. v. 11. 12: ita ut in utroque Testam. eadem sit fœderis promissio: Ero Deus tuus: & Baptizo te in nomine P. F. Sp. S. Sicut ergo in Isaaco puerulo præcessit Circumcisio, sigillum justitiæ: postea verò crescente ætate, & ipso in pietate instituto, fides actualis & conversio vitæ secuta fuit: eadem est ratio Baptismi parvulorum. Licet enim infantes per ætatem non capaces sint fidei actualis, pœnitentiæ & regenerationis: Baptismi tamen efficacia non ad primum illum vel diem vel annum adstricta est: sed semen illud Spiritus S. in cordibus electorum, tempore definito adolescet & fructificabit. Unde infantes quâ electi, rectè dicuntur habere semen fidei & sanctificationis, per gratiosam illam & extraordinariam operationem Spi. S. Psal. 22. v. 10. 11.
units.tr: It is further proved from the sacrament of circumcision, to which baptism in the New Testament succeeded in substance, with the ceremonies and accidents set aside. Col. 2:11, 12. So in both Testaments the promise of the covenant is the same: "I will be your God," and "I baptize you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit." Just as in the little boy Isaac circumcision came first, as the seal of righteousness, and afterwards, as he grew in age and was instructed in piety, actual faith and a change of life followed, so the reason for infant baptism is the same. For although infants, by reason of their age, are not capable of actual faith, repentance and regeneration, the efficacy of baptism is not bound to that first day or year. Rather, that seed of the Holy Spirit in the hearts of the elect will grow and bear fruit at a set time. Hence infants, as elect, are rightly said to have the seed of faith and sanctification, through that gracious and extraordinary operation of the Holy Spirit. Ps. 22:10, 11.

units.la: THESIS XXVII.
units.tr: THESIS XXVII.

units.la: Denique Baptismus, cûm sit pars ministerij Ecclesiastici, Matth. 28. v. 19. Mar. 16. v. 16, non ergo per aniculas, obstetrices trices, nec per alias personas ad Leiturgiam Ecclesiasticam non vocatas, sed per ministros ordinarios administrari debet, ut omnia in Ecclesia Dei peragantur ἐυτάχτως κ) ἐυφχη-μόνως. 1. Cor. 14. v. 40.
units.tr: Finally, since Baptism is part of the ministry of the Church (Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:16), it ought not to be administered by old women or midwives, nor by any other persons not called to the ecclesiastical liturgy, but by the ordinary ministers, so that all things in the Church of God are done decently and in order (1 Cor. 14:40).

units.la: 1. Necessitatis casus circa obstetricum baptismum est fictitius. Cum enim salus hominis dependeat à fœdere Dei per Christum Mediatorem sancito: Sacramenta vero tantum sint appendices & sigilla fœderis: Quicunque ergo vel mortis necessitate divinitus impositâ, vel gravi aliquâ persecutione grassante, externo Baptismate per Pastorem idoneum administrando destituuntur, illi tamen, quâ electi sunt filij Dei, per sanguinem Christi à peccatis abluuntur & per Spiritum Sanctum ad regnum Dei regenerantur, extraordinarie. 2. Et licet hoc officium commune omnibus Christianis, cujuscunque sint sexus & ordinis, incumbat, ut sese mutuò ex Dei Verbo instituant, corrigant & consolentur, juxta legem charitatis Christianæ: Attamen cum administratio Sacramentorum sit pars legationis Ecclesiasticæ, quæ solis ad munus hoc sacrum legitimè vocatis convenit; ergo non nisi ijs, qui nomine Christi legatione funguntur, competit. 2. Cor. 5. v. 20. Hebr. 5. v. 4.
units.tr: 1. The case of necessity invoked for lay or midwife baptism is fictitious. For since a person's salvation depends on the covenant of God sealed through Christ the Mediator, and the sacraments are only appendages and seals of the covenant, whoever is deprived of external baptism, to be administered by a suitable minister, either by the necessity of death imposed by God or by some grave persecution raging around them, is nevertheless washed from sins by the blood of Christ and regenerated by the Holy Spirit into the kingdom of God, in an extraordinary way, insofar as they are elect children of God. 2. And although this duty lies upon all Christians, of whatever sex or rank, to instruct, correct and console one another from the Word of God according to the law of Christian love, nevertheless, since the administration of the sacraments is part of the ecclesiastical embassy, which belongs only to those lawfully called to this sacred office, it therefore pertains only to those who discharge the embassy in the name of Christ (2 Cor. 5:20; Heb. 5:4).

units.la: CAPUT CONFESSIONIS HELVETICAE XXI.
units.tr: Chapter 21 of the Helvetic Confession.

units.la: De Sacra Cœna Domini.
units.tr: On the Holy Supper of the Lord.

units.la: THESIS XXVIII.
units.tr: THESIS XXVIII.

units.la: Eucharistia est alterum Sacramentum Novi Testa-mentum, quo Dominus nobis panem ac vinum benedictum, cum fideli mortis suæ recordatione sumentibus, testificatur & obsignat, se corpore suo pro nobis tradito & sanguine effuso, animas nostras ita pascere & vivificare, ut cum ipso capite nostro & inter nos, in unum corpus coalescamus; fcamus; atque fœdus in Baptismo cum Deo initum, ita per-petuò ratum inter nos conservetur.
units.tr: The Eucharist is the second Sacrament of the New Testament, by which the Lord testifies to us and seals, to those who take the blessed bread and wine with a faithful remembrance of his death, that he nourishes and quickens our souls with his body given for us and his blood shed, so that we are joined together into one body with our Head himself and among ourselves; and that the covenant entered into with God in Baptism is thus kept ratified and preserved among us for ever.

units.la: THESIS XXIX.
units.tr: THESIS XXIX.

units.la: Esus & potus carnis & sanguinis Christi, de quo Iohan. 6. agitur, convenit quoad substantiam cum illo, quem cæ-teri Evangelistæ, in S. Cœnæ institutione Dominica descri-bunt; quia utrobique eadem caro & idem sanguis Christi, in nutritionem animæ ad vitam æternam, fidelibus promit-titur & exhibetur. Differunt autem ratione accidentis: quia ille purè spiritualis, usu Symbolico destitutus, etiam extra S. Cœnam, ex promissionis Evangelicæ auditu & consi-deratione fideli participatur: Hic vero ritu Sacramentali vestitus, maioris ἀσφαλείας causâ sanctus est. Orthodoxi pa-tres judicaverunt, S. Iohannem ideò nullam institutionis S. Cœnæ mentionem fecisse, sicut cæteri Evangelistæ: quia cap. 6. plenius de fructu istius esus & potus, disseruerit. Ioh 6. cap. Christus nullâ mentionem fecit panis materialis, calicis, gratiarum actionis, fracti-onis, distributionis, commemorationis, Testamenti, quæ omnia ad esu & potu symbolicu spectat. Panis, de quo Dominus locutus est Ioh. 6. ca. non est panis S. Cœnæ, sed est ipsius Domini Christi caro, quæ panis appellatur metaphoricè, & quæ extra usum S. Cœnæ spiritua-liter per fidè participatur. Hujusmodi esus & potus apprimè salutaris est ijs, qui in persecutionibus ministerio Ecclesiastico prorsus or-bati sunt, promissioni tamen Evangelicæ de Christo mortuo & resu-scitato, ita ex corde credunt, ut anima ipsorum per Salvatoris sui meritum efficaciter ad vitam æternam nutriatur.
units.tr: The eating and drinking of the flesh and blood of Christ, of which Iohan. 6. speaks, agrees in substance with that which the other Evangelists describe in the institution of the Lord's Supper, since in both the same flesh and the same blood of Christ are promised and exhibited to believers for the nourishment of the soul unto eternal life. They differ, however, in the manner of the accident: the former is purely spiritual, lacks any symbolic use, and is received by faith even outside the Lord's Supper, from hearing and meditating on the Gospel promise; the latter is clothed in a sacramental rite and is holy for the sake of greater safety [ἀσφαλείας]. The orthodox Fathers judged that John therefore made no mention of the institution of the Lord's Supper, as the other Evangelists did, because in chapter 6 he discussed more fully the fruit of this eating and drinking. In John 6 Christ made no mention of material bread, of the cup, of the giving of thanks, the breaking, the distribution, the commemoration, or the Testament, all of which pertain to symbolic eating and drinking. The bread of which the Lord spoke in John 6 is not the bread of the Lord's Supper but the very flesh of the Lord Christ, which is called bread metaphorically and which is spiritually received through faith outside the use of the Lord's Supper. This kind of eating and drinking is especially salutary for those who, in persecutions, have been completely deprived of the ministry of the Church, yet who believe from the heart the Evangelical promise concerning Christ dead and risen, so that their soul is effectively nourished unto eternal life through the merit of their Saviour.

units.la: THESIS XXX.
units.tr: THESIS XXX.

units.la: Obiectum, in quo corporis & sanguinis Christi mandu-catio & potio spiritualis determinatur, non est tantùm Spi-ritus Christi vivificus vel eius Divinitas; nedum imagina-rius aliquis cibus & potus; nec efficacia tantum, seu me-rita & effecta passionis & mortis Christi: sed ipsius verum corpus pro peccatis mundi immolatum; & verus ipsius sanguis, in λύτρον redemptionis nostræ in cruce effusus. De eodem & eodem objecto Dominus utrobique locutus est. Matth. 26. Accipite, comedite, hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur: sanguis qui pro vobis effunditur. Ioh. 6. v. 51. Ego sum panis ille vitæ, qui de cœlo descendi: Panis quem ego dabo, caro mea est. Caro mea est veré cibus; & sanguis meus veré est potus. Obiectum saluti�feri esus & potus appellatur Spirituale, non ratione substantiæ, quasi caro & sanguis Christi sint substantia incorporea, spiritualis, invisibilis: sed quia ista participatio fit operatione Spiritus San-ctí, instrumento spirituali, quod est fides: & respectu sui finis & usus, qui ad vitam spiritualem, cœlestem & æternam spectat.
units.tr: The object in which the eating and drinking of the body and blood of Christ are spiritually determined is not merely the life-giving Spirit of Christ or his Divinity, still less some imaginary food and drink, nor only the efficacy, that is, the merits and effects of the passion and death of Christ; it is his true body, offered for the sins of the world, and his true blood, poured out on the cross as the ransom [λύτρον] of our redemption. Concerning this same object, the Lord spoke in both cases. Matt. 26: "Take, eat; this is my body, which is given for you; this is the blood which is shed for you." John 6:51: "I am that living bread which came down from heaven. The bread that I will give is my flesh. My flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink." The food and drink of salvation is called spiritual not because of its substance, as if the flesh and blood of Christ were an incorporeal, spiritual, invisible substance, but because this participation takes place through the working of the Holy Spirit, by a spiritual instrument, which is faith, and because of its end and use, which looks to spiritual, heavenly and eternal life.

units.la: THESIS XXXI.
units.tr: THESIS XXXI.

units.la: Orthodoxiæ igitur absona est istorum sententia, qui meri-ta & effecta mortis Christi, ab ipsius corpore & sanguine, in victimam expiatoriam oblato, separant & divellunt. Nemo enim beneficiorum Christi, remissionis peccatorum, ustitiæ sempiternæ, regenerationis item per Spiritum San-ctum, & glorificationis ad vitam æternam, particeps fieri poterit, nisi priùs quoque cum Christo capite, in unitate corporis, spiritualiter coniunctus fuerit. Sicuti enim palmi-tes non possunt á radice vitis, succum vitalem attrahere, nedum florescere & fructum proferre, sed necessario exarescunt, nisi ipsi trunco vitis fuerint insiti: Eadem est ratio membrorum corporis Christi. Iohan. 15. Errant igitur Adversarij, qui statuunt homines fidei & pœnitentiæ gratiâ destitutos, participare Sacramentali & spirituali quodam modo, verum Christi corpus & sanguinem: mo-do autem mystico & veré Spirituali eos non participes fieri benefi-ciorum, quæ Christus corpore & sanguine suo nobis acquisiverit: ubicunque enim corpus Christi est, ibi vivificum est: & vivificam virtutem suam nunquam amittit. Ioh. 6. 53. Nisi ederitis carnem filij hominis & biberitis ejus sanguinem non habebitis vitam in vobis.
units.tr: Therefore the opinion of those is out of tune with orthodoxy, who separate and tear apart the merits and effects of Christ's death from his body and blood offered as an expiatory sacrifice. For no one can become a partaker of the benefits of Christ (remission of sins, everlasting righteousness, likewise regeneration through the Holy Spirit, and glorification unto eternal life) unless he has first also been spiritually joined to Christ the Head, in the unity of the body. For just as branches cannot draw vital sap from the root of the vine, much less flourish and bear fruit, but necessarily wither unless they have been grafted into the trunk of the vine itself, so it is with the members of Christ's body (John 15). Those adversaries therefore err, who maintain that men destitute of faith and repentance participate in the true body and blood of Christ in a sacramental and certain spiritual manner, but not in a mystical and truly spiritual manner, so that they do not become partakers of the benefits which Christ has acquired for us by his body and blood. For wherever the body of Christ is, there it is life-giving, and it never loses its life-giving power (John 6:53): "Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you."

units.la: THESIS XXXII.
units.tr: THESIS XXXII.

units.la: Cúm verò corpus & sanguis Christi, cibus & potus sint non ventris, sed animæ ad vitam æternam: ergo non nisi organo spirituali, quod animæ conveniens est, participatur. Hoc organon est sola fides, peculiari efficacia Spiritus Sancti excitata, quæ metaphoricè Os & Manus & Oculus animæ appellatur.
units.tr: Since the body and blood of Christ are food and drink not for the belly but for the soul, unto eternal life, they are received only by a spiritual organ, one fitting the soul. This organ is faith alone, roused by the peculiar efficacy of the Holy Spirit, which is metaphorically called the mouth, the hand, and the eye of the soul.

units.la: Ioh. 6. v. 35. 51. 56. 57. Ego sum panis ille vitæ, qui venit ad me, non esuriet unquam; & qui crediderit in me, is non sitiet in æternum. Et, Qui ederit me, is vivet propter me, & manebit in me, & ego in ipso. Ephes. 3. 17. Per fidem habitat Christus in cordibus nostris.
units.tr: John 6:35, 51, 56, 57. I am that bread of life; he who comes to me shall never hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst for ever. And: He who eats me, the same shall live by me, and shall abide in me, and I in him. Eph. 3:17. Christ dwells in our hearts through faith.

units.la: Quemadmodum interna & spiritualis substantia cujuslibet Sacramenti, á solo Deo offertur & exhibetur, non á ministro Ecclesiæ: Et offertur non sensibus & organis corporis, sed fidei tantùm: Ita quoque non nisi fide percipitur. Ioh. 6. v. 32. Non Moses dedit vobis panem illum de cælis: verùm Pater meus dat vobis panem illum ἀληθινὸν de cælo. Nullum spirituale bonum á Deo promissum, sive in Verbo sive in Sacramentis, absque fide percipi potest: Promissio absque fide non est firma. Rom. 4. v. 16.
units.tr: Just as the inward and spiritual substance of any sacrament is offered and exhibited by God alone, not by the minister of the Church, and is offered not to the senses and bodily organs but to faith only, so likewise it is received only by faith. John 6:32. Moses did not give you that bread from heaven; but my Father gives you the true [ἀληθινὸν] bread from heaven. No spiritual good promised by God, whether in the Word or in the Sacraments, can be received without faith; a promise without faith is not firm. Rom. 4:16.

units.la: THESIS XXXIII.
units.tr: THESIS XXXIII.

units.la: Propterea soli fideles & pœnitentes, corpus & sanguinem Christi participant. Eius modi enim pretiosa & salutaria dona, hisce solis hæredibus in Testamento Christi legata sunt. Cæteri verò qui hoc applicationis instrumento sunt destituti, etiamsi signa externa participent, non possunt tamen ipsius substantiæ Christi participes reddi. Indignè quidem manducates & bibentes fiunt rei corporis & sanguinis Christi, nō tamen quód illa ore suo percipiāt, sed quia turpis sipis sigillorum Testamenti abusus & contemptus redundat in ipsum quoque Testatorem Christum; non minús quám diplomatum publicorum violatores,non tantúm in violati signi sacri ,verúm etiam in ipsius Maiestatis læsæ crimen incurrunt.
units.tr: Therefore only believers and penitents partake of the body and blood of Christ. For such precious and saving gifts have been bequeathed in the Testament of Christ to these heirs alone. The rest, however, who lack this instrument of application, even if they partake of the external signs, cannot nevertheless be made partakers of the very substance of Christ. Those who eat and drink unworthily indeed become guilty of the body and blood of Christ, yet not because they receive those things with their mouth, but because the shameful abuse and contempt of the seals of the Testament rebounds upon Christ the Testator himself; just as violators of public documents incur not only the guilt of violating the sacred seal but also the crime of injured majesty itself.

units.la: Ioh.3. v.18.36. Qui non credit, jam condemnatus est, & ira Dei manet super ipsum. 1. Cor.11. v.27. 29. Qui indignè edunt & bibunt, rei fiunt corporis & sanguinis Christi; damnationem sibiipsis edunt & bibunt, non discernentes corpus Domini. Item, Evangelium de Christo est odor mortis ad mortem ijs qui pereunt : alijs verò qui servantur, odor vitæ ad vitam. 2. Cor.2. v.15.16. Hebr.10. v.29. Quantò acerbiore supplicio dignus censebitur, qui Filium Dei conculcârit, & sanguinem fœderis, per quem fuerat sanctificatus, profanum duxerit, & Spiritum gratiæ contumeliâ affecerit?
units.tr: John 3:18, 36. He who does not believe is already condemned, and the wrath of God remains upon him. 1 Cor. 11:27, 29. Whoever eats and drinks unworthily becomes guilty of the body and blood of the Lord; they eat and drink judgment to themselves, not discerning the body of the Lord. Likewise, the Gospel of Christ is a savour of death unto death to those who perish, but to those who are saved a savour of life unto life. 2 Cor. 2:15, 16. Heb. 10:29. How much worse a punishment will he be judged worthy of, who has trodden underfoot the Son of God, and counted the blood of the covenant, by which he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

units.la: Licet fides non ingrediatur substantiæ Sacramentalis constitutionem; attamen ad salutarem efficaciam, usum & perfruitionem ejus, necessariò requiritur. Nullius Sacramenti legitimus usus sine fide participantis consistere potest. Sacramenta enim non propter infideles, sed propter fideles instituta sunt, ut hi Christum cum omnibus ejus benefactis, efficaciùs sibi applicarent, arctiúsque cum eo coalescerent. Sententia Pauli Rom.3. v.3. Fides Dei non enervatur per hominum incredulitatem; non patrocinatur ijs qui circa usum Sacramentorum, nullâ fidei & pœnitentiæ gratiâ præditi sunt: verúm intelligi debet de fœderis divini constantia erga electos, quorum graves lapsus efficere nequeant, quó minús Deus sua promissa ipsis præstet.
units.tr: Although faith does not enter into the constitution of the sacramental substance, nevertheless it is necessarily required for its saving efficacy, its use and its enjoyment. The lawful use of no sacrament can exist without the faith of the one who partakes. For the sacraments were instituted not for unbelievers but for believers, so that these might apply Christ with all his benefits to themselves more effectively and cleave more closely to him. The saying of Paul, Rom. 3:3: "The faithfulness of God is not made void by the unbelief of men," does not lend support to those who, though endowed with no faith or grace of repentance, are concerned with the use of the sacraments; it must be understood of the constancy of the divine covenant towards the elect, whose grievous falls cannot prevent God from fulfilling his promises to them.

units.la: THESIS XXXIV.
units.tr: THESIS XXXIV.

units.la: Asserimus Patres Veteris Testam, quotquot ab origine mundi vixerunt, corpore & sanguine Christi, spiritualiter nobiscum nutritos fuisse ad vitam æternam. Etsi enim natura Christi humana tum nondum fueritin rerum naturara : ratione tamen promissionis divinæ & typorum Sacramentalium Verbo annexorum, credentibus præsens fuit. Hæc enim est veræ fidei natura, vis & proprietas, ut Deum ipsum in verbo promissionis intueatur, itaut licet nondum in rerum natura existat id, quod animæ fideli à Deo promissum est, vel intervallis locorum & temporum procul adhuc sit positum, tamen virtute Dei sit ipsi præsentissimum. Fides enim est ὑπόστασις τῶν ἐλπιζομένων, ἔλεγχος τῶν μὴ βλεπομένων. Promissiones divinæ, quibus fides innititur, sunt Gen. 3. Gen. 12. v. 3. Gal 3. v. 16. Iohan. 8. v. 56. Actor. 10. 43. Actor. 15. 11. 1. Cor. 10. v. 4. Hebr. 13. v. 8. Apoc. 13. v. 8. agnus ab origine mundi mactatus. Vide exegesin Theseos 13.
units.tr: We assert that the Fathers of the Old Testament, as many as lived from the beginning of the world, were spiritually nourished with the body and blood of Christ unto eternal life, just as we are. For although the human nature of Christ did not yet exist in the nature of things, nevertheless by the force of the divine promise and of the sacramental types annexed to the Word, he was present to believers. For this is the nature, power and property of true faith: that it looks upon God himself in the word of promise, so that, although that which God has promised to the faithful soul does not yet exist in the nature of things, or is still far off in the distance of places and times, nevertheless by the power of God it is most present to it. For faith is "the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen" [ὑπόστασις τῶν ἐλπιζομένων, ἔλεγχος τῶν μὴ βλεπομένων]. The divine promises on which faith rests are Gen. 3; Gen. 12. 3; Gal. 3. 16; John 8. 56; Acts 10. 43; Acts 15. 11; 1 Cor. 10. 4; Heb. 13. 8; Rev. 13. 8, "the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world." See the exegesis of Thesis 13.

units.la: THESIS XXXV.
units.tr: THESIS XXXV.

units.la: Oralem verò manducationem carnis suæ, Christus in Evangelio nusquam promisit, nedum sacramento Cœnæ eam sancivit, verùm expresis argumentis reiecit Iohan. 6. Corpus igitur & sanguinem suum, non in pane vel in specie panis, sed Verbo promissionis fide manducandum & bibendum exhibet. Ioh. 6. v. 27. Operemini cibum, non illum qui perit, sed cibum illum qui permanet ad vitam æternam, quem Filius hominis dabit vobis. Ioh. 6. v. 62. 63. Quid si spectaveritis Filium hominis ascendentem eo ubi prius erat? Spiritus est qui vivificat: caro non prodest quicquam: verba quæ loquor vobis, Spiritus sunt & vita sunt. Adversarij manducationem Oralem & Sacramentalem, pro eadem accipiunt perperam. Sacramentalis enim distingui debet, pro diverso suo objecto. In legitimo ejus usu, pij percipiunt ore corporis signa Sacramentalia, fide autem rem quoque significatam. Impij fide destituti, participant symbola tantùm: Oralem vel corporalem manducationem fingunt adversarij, quâ omnes communicantes promiscuè participent ipsum verum corpus & sanguinem Christi, quod absurdum, cùm nullus corporalis esus & potus nutrire possit Spiritum hominis ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Christ nowhere promises in the Gospel an oral eating of his flesh, much less sanctions it in the sacrament of the Supper; rather, by clear arguments he rejects it (John 6). He therefore offers his body and blood to be eaten and drunk not in the bread, or under the form of bread, but by faith in the word of promise. John 6:27: Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you. John 6:62-63: What and if ye shall see the Son of man ascend up where he was before? It is the Spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life. Our opponents wrongly take oral and sacramental eating to be the same thing. Sacramental eating must be distinguished according to its different object. In its lawful use, the godly receive the sacramental signs with the mouth of the body, but by faith they also receive the thing signified. The unbelieving, destitute of faith, partake of the symbols only. Our opponents invent an oral or bodily eating, by which all communicants indiscriminately partake of the very true body and blood of Christ; this is absurd, since no bodily eating and drinking can nourish the spirit of man to eternal life.

units.la: THESIS XXXVI.
units.tr: THESIS XXXVI.

units.la: Ex spirituali corporis & sanguinis Christi participatione, de eiusdem in sacra Eucharistia præsentiâ iudicari potest. Cum enim Christi caro & sanguis á credentibus veré manducetur & bibatur, veré præsens adsit necesse est: non quidem pani & vino, sed hominibus credentibus & Sacramento legitimé utentibus, præsens. Cumque applicatio Christi non fiat ore, sed fide; præsentia ergo non corporalis, sed spiritualis, necessariò sequitur. Christus corpore & sanguine suo realiter præsens est, non respectu existentiæ localis, nec corporaliter, sed spiritualiter: Hæc vera & realis præsentia nititur fundamento promissionis divinæ, quâ Dominus in S. Cœnæ institutione, esum & potum sui corporis & sanguinis, fidelibus promisit; & promissionem illam certissimé præstabit. Unde etiam emergit talis UNIO Sacramentalis, de qua supra dictum, quâ Signum & res Signata, per institutionem, promissionem & efficaciam divinam, in legitimo usu conjuncta sunt. Corporalis verò Christi præsentia pugnat cum institutione Cœnæ, in qua non corporalis sed spiritualis cibus nobis promissus; cum veritate corporis Christi, quod nostro est consubstantiale. Luc. 24. Heb. 2; Cum natura omnium Sacramentorum, in quibus res signata non aliter est præsens, quám spiritualiter per fidem.
units.tr: From the spiritual participation in the body and blood of Christ, one can judge of his presence in the holy Eucharist. For since the flesh and blood of Christ are truly eaten and drunk by believers, he must truly be present: present not to the bread and wine, but to believers who use the sacrament lawfully. And since the application of Christ is made not by the mouth but by faith, a presence that is not bodily but spiritual necessarily follows. Christ is really present with his body and blood, not in respect of local existence, nor bodily, but spiritually. This true and real presence rests on the foundation of the divine promise, by which the Lord, in the institution of the Holy Supper, promised the faithful the eating and drinking of his body and blood, and he will most certainly fulfil that promise. Hence also emerges that sacramental UNION of which we spoke above, by which the sign and the thing signified are joined together, through the institution, promise and divine efficacy, in lawful use. But a bodily presence of Christ conflicts with the institution of the Supper, in which a spiritual and not a bodily food is promised to us; it conflicts with the truth of Christ's body, which is consubstantial with ours; and it conflicts with the nature of all sacraments, in which the thing signified is present in no other way than spiritually, through faith. Luc. 24. Heb. 2;

units.la: THESIS XXXVII.
units.tr: THESIS XXXVII.

units.la: Denique præsentiam Christi in sacra Cœna credimus, non solius Deitatis respectu; verùm etiam corporis & sanguinis eiusdem ratione: præsentiam tamen & communionem spiritualem, cuius gratiâ universa Verbi & Sacramentorum Oeconomia instituta est.
units.tr: Finally, we believe that Christ is present in the holy Supper not only with respect to his Deity but also in respect of his body and blood. Yet the spiritual presence and communion, for the sake of which the whole economy of the Word and the Sacraments was instituted, is the chief thing.

units.la: Quæcunque præsentia & communicatio promittitur Verbo, eadem quoq; obsignatur Sacramentis: & é contrario; item qualis est præsentia & communio in S. Baptismo; talis quoque est in S. Cœna; na; & vicissim: At in Baptismo tantum est spiritualis. 1. Cor. 12. v. 13. Per unum Spiritum in unum corpus baptizati sumus. Quae praesentia pugnat cum articulis fidei, de incarnatione Filij Dei; de circūscripta veritate assumpti corporis humani; de unione personali naturae humanae cum ὑποστάσει τῷ λόγῳ; de adscensione Christi in caelos; de Sessione ejus ad dextram Patris in caelis, &c. ea est falsa.
units.tr: Whatever presence and communion is promised in the Word, the same is also sealed in the Sacraments; and conversely. Likewise, such as the presence and communion is in holy Baptism, such also is it in the holy Supper; and vice versa. But in Baptism it is only spiritual. 1 Cor. 12. v. 13: By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body. That presence, which contradicts the articles of faith concerning the incarnation of the Son of God; concerning the circumscribed truth of the assumed human body; concerning the personal union of the human nature with the hypostasis of the Word [ὑποστάσει τῷ λόγῳ]; concerning the ascension of Christ into the heavens; concerning his sitting at the right hand of the Father in heaven, etc., is false.

units.la: Et haec Totius Christi τῷ Διαυθρώπῳ praesentia spiritualis, non est imaginaria & phantastica, ut adversarij calumniantur; quasi nihil verum & reale sit, nisi quod carnale, terrenum, & ipsis impijs quoque commune; sed vera est atque per Spiritum Sanctum efficax, quae consistit in caelesti & mystica nostri ceu membrorum cum capite communione, ad quam nullo de caelis descensu nec visibili nec invisibili opus est: Sicut & nobis, qui ejus membra sumus mystica, non opus est adscensu Physico in caelos, ut cum ipso capite nostro arctius conjungamur. Praesentior enim est is, qui se ipse animis nostris inserit, quam qui oculis praesens exhibetur, quia plus est mente connecti, quam corpore copulari: plus est Christum intus habere in CORDE, quam in ORE. In promptu sunt promissiones illae luculentae: Ioh. 6. v. 35. Qui venit ad me, & qui credit in me, non sitiet & esuriet unquam. v. 56. 57. Is in me manet, & ego in eo: & ipse quoque vivet per me. Ioh. 14. v. 23. Pater meus & ego veniemus ad eum & apud eum manebimus. Eph. 3. 17. Per fidem inhabitat Christus in cordibus vestris. 1. Ioh. 3. v. 24. Per hoc novimus, eum habitare in nobis, nempe ex Spiritu, quem dedit nobis.
units.tr: And this spiritual presence of the whole God-man [θεανθρώπου] is not imaginary or fantastical, as the adversaries slander, as if nothing were true and real except what is carnal, earthly, and common even to the wicked. It is true and, through the Holy Spirit, effective. It consists in the heavenly and mystical communion of us, as members, with the Head, and for this no descent from heaven, either visible or invisible, is needed. Just as we, who are his mystical members, have no need of a physical ascent into heaven in order to be joined more closely to our Head himself. For he is more present who inserts himself into our minds than he who is exhibited present to our eyes, since it is more to be joined in mind than to be coupled in body; it is more to have Christ within in the HEART than in the MOUTH. The clear promises are at hand: John 6. v. 35: He who comes to me and believes in me shall never hunger or thirst. vv. 56, 57: He who abides in me, and I in him; and he shall also live through me. John 14. v. 23: My Father and I will come to him and make our abode with him. Eph. 3. 17: Christ dwells in your hearts through faith. 1 John 3. v. 24: By this we know that he abides in us, namely by the Spirit whom he has given us.

units.la: Plane ἄτοπον est, quod Vbiquetarij Corpori Christi tribuunt res alicubi essendi modos. Primum circumscriptivum seu corporalem, secundum trinam corporis dimensionem, localem, visibilem, juxta quem modum DN. Christus in statu exinanitionis versatus, corpore suo Hierosolymae, Bethaniae, &c. certis in locis fuerit praesens. Alterum modum definitivum, qui Angelis & Spiritibus proprie competit, secundum quem Christus maxime in statu exaltationis, corpore invisibili & per dimensiones penetrabili, spiritualles proprietates obtinente, pluribus in locis simul esse potuerit; quo per clausum sepulchrum exiverit ; per clausas januas ad discipulos ingressus sit ; é conspectu discipulorum Emaunte evanuerit, &c. Tertium modum appellant repletivum, divinum, cœlestem, majestaticum, á gloria dexteræ Dei dependentem ; secundúm quem corpus Christi ad dextram Patris exaltati sit omnipraesens, juxta illud: Matth. 18. 20. Vbi duo aut tres: Matth. 28. 20. Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad seculi consummationem. Eph. 4. 10. Adscendit super omnes cœlos, ut impleret omnia. In quo triplici præsentiæ modo plurima confusa, ἀσίσκατα, contra dicta toria, in voluta sunt.
units.tr: Plainly it is absurd [ἄτοπον] that the Ubiquitarians ascribe to the body of Christ modes of being somewhere. The first is the circumscriptive or corporeal mode, according to the threefold dimension of a body, local and visible, by which mode our Lord Christ, while he lived in the state of humiliation, was present with his body in certain places, at Jerusalem, at Bethany, etc. The second is the definitive mode, which properly belongs to angels and spirits, according to which Christ, especially in the state of exaltation, with an invisible body penetrable by dimensions and possessing spiritual properties, could be in several places at once; by it he came out of the closed sepulchre, entered to the disciples through closed doors, and vanished from the sight of the disciples at Emmaus, etc. They call the third mode the repletive, divine, heavenly, majestic mode, depending on the glory of the right hand of God; according to it the body of Christ, exalted at the right hand of the Father, is omnipresent, in line with that saying: Matt. 18. 20: Where two or three are gathered; Matt. 28. 20: Behold, I am with you all days, even to the end of the world; Eph. 4. 10: He ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things. In this threefold mode of presence a great deal is confused, inconsistent [ἀσίσκατα], and contradictory.

units.la: Captiosæ sunt eorundem rationes, ab unione personali desumptæ: quód λόγος totus sit in carne assumpta, & extra carnem nulli libi; quód duæ naturæ in Christo indistanter unitæ sint. Quæ sophismata cum Verbo Dei & Symbolis orthodoxarum Synodorum diserté pugnant. Vnio enim personæ τῶ λόγῳ assumentis & humanæ naturæ assumptæ, facta est ratione proprietatum essentialium utriúsque naturæ, ἀσυγχύτως ἡ ἀτρέπτως, inconfusé & immutabiliter: ἀδιαιρέτως ἡ ἀχωρίστως, indivisé & inseparabiliter. Et qualis est unio utriúsque naturæ, mediante personâ, talis quoque est communio proprietatum in persona τῶ λόγῳ, videl. omniscientiæ, omnipræsentiæ, omnipotentiæ, &c. non quod unius naturæ idiomata transfundantur in alteram, sed potiús utriusque naturæ proprietates de persona, ex duabus naturis constante prædicentur. Vnde absurdissimæ consequentiæ eliciuntur, quando idiomata unius naturæ non tribuuntur Personæ, voce concreta, ab altera natura denominatæ (Filius Dei est ex Maria natus, passus, mortuus: Filius hominis est prior Abrahamo. Ioh. 8. Filius hominis loquens in terris, fuit in cœlo. Ioh. 3.) sed prædicantur de altera natura, voce abstracta; Deitas τῶ λόγῳ est passa, mortua: caro Christi est omnipræsens, &c.
units.tr: Their arguments are captious, drawn from the personal union: that the Word is wholly in the assumed flesh and nowhere outside the flesh; that the two natures in Christ are united without distinction. These sophisms plainly clash with the Word of God and with the creeds of the orthodox synods. For the union of the person of the assuming Word and the assumed human nature was made, by reason of the essential properties of each nature, without confusion and unchangeably [ἀσυγχύτως ἢ ἀτρέπτως], indivisibly and inseparably [ἀδιαιρέτως ἢ ἀχωρίστως]. And as is the union of the two natures through the person, so too is the communion of properties in the person of the Word, namely of omniscience, omnipresence, omnipotence, etc. This is not because the attributes of one nature are poured into the other, but rather because the properties of each nature are predicated of the person who consists of the two natures. Hence the most absurd consequences follow when the attributes of one nature are not ascribed to the Person named by a concrete term derived from the other nature (The Son of God was born of Mary, suffered, died; The Son of man was before Abraham, John 8. The Son of man, speaking on earth, was in heaven, John 3.), but are predicated of the other nature by an abstract term: the Deity of the Word suffered and died; the flesh of Christ is omnipresent, etc.

units.la: DENIQUE inanes sunt prætextus rationum, quas depromunt ab Omnipotentia Dei, ubi de ejus voluntate ex Verbo revelato non priús constat, præsertim in ejusmodi assertionibus, quæ sum. cum veritate, justitia & potentia Dei pugnant. A miraculoso item Dei opere, quod cum Sacramento Eucharistiae perpetuo sit conjunctum. Christum ajunt adesse miraculose, non obstantibus articulis: de proprietate corporis humani a Christo personaliter assumpti: de adscensione Christi visibili, &c. atque ita Sacramentum familiare in miraculum Consubstantiationis & Transsubstantiationis falso convertunt.
units.tr: Finally, the pretexts of the arguments they draw from the omnipotence of God are empty, where his will is not first established from the revealed Word, especially in such assertions as contradict the truth, justice and power of God. Likewise they appeal to a miraculous work of God, which is perpetually joined with the Sacrament of the Eucharist. They say that Christ is present miraculously, notwithstanding the articles concerning the properties of the human body personally assumed by Christ, and concerning the visible ascension of Christ, etc. And thus they falsely turn the familiar Sacrament into the miracle of Consubstantiation and Transubstantiation.

units.la: CORONIS.
units.tr: CORONIS.

units.la: An & quo sensu Eucharistia sit Sacrificium? De Transsubstantiatione; De Sacrificio Missae expiatorio, pro peccatis viventium & mortuorum; De Canone Missae. De communione sub utraque specie. De adoratione hostiae. De reservatione hostiae consecratae. De Leiturgiis Veterum. De Altaribus, &c.
units.tr: Whether and in what sense the Eucharist is a sacrifice? On Transubstantiation; on the expiatory sacrifice of the Mass for the sins of the living and the dead; on the Canon of the Mass; on communion under both kinds; on the adoration of the host; on the reservation of the consecrated host; on the liturgies of the ancients; on altars, etc.

units.la: Peculiaris Diatribe proxime, Deo votis nostris aspirante, instituetur.
units.tr: A separate treatise will be undertaken shortly, God willing, with our prayers assisting.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: FINIS.
